blocks.en: Early in April of 1958, my wife and I arrived, malarial and diffident, in a Balinese village we intended, as anthropologists, to study. A small place, about five hundred people, and relatively remote, it was its own world. We were intruders, professional ones, and the villagers dealt with us as Balinese seem always to deal with people not part of their life who yet press themselves upon them: as though we were not there. For them, and to a degree for ourselves, we were nonpersons, specters, invisible men.
blocks.zh: 1958 年 4 月初，我和妻子带着疟疾和羞怯来到巴厘岛的一个村庄，我们打算作为人类学家进行研究。地方不大，五百人左右，又比较偏僻，却是一片自己的天地。我们是入侵者，是专业人士，村民们对待我们就像巴厘人对待我们一样，似乎总是对待那些不属于他们生活的人，但他们却向他们施加压力：就好像我们不在那里一样。对于他们来说，在某种程度上对于我们自己来说，我们都是非人、幽灵、隐形人。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: We moved into an extended family compound (that had been arranged before through the provincial government) belonging to one of the four major factions in village life. But except for our landlord and the village chief, whose cousin and brother-in-law he was, everyone ignored us in a way only a Balinese can do. As we wandered around, uncertain, wistful, eager to please, people seemed to look right through us with a gaze focused several yards behind us on some more actual stone or tree. Almost nobody greeted us; but nobody scowled or said anything unpleasant to us either, which would have been almost as satisfactory. If we ventured to approach someone (something one is powerfully inhibited from doing in such an atmosphere), he moved, negligently but definitively, away. If, seated or leaning against a wall, we had him trapped, he said nothing at all, or mumbled what for the Balinese is the ultimate nonword– “yes.” The indifference, of course, was studied; the villagers were watching every move we made and they had an enormous amount of quite accurate information about who we were and what we were going to be doing. But they acted as if we simply did not exist, which, in fact, as this behavior was designed to inform us, we did not, or anyway not yet.
blocks.zh: 我们搬进了一个大家庭大院（之前是通过省政府安排的），属于乡村生活的四大派别之一。但除了我们的房东和村长（他是他的表弟和妹夫）之外，每个人都忽视我们，只有巴厘岛人才能做到这一点。当我们四处闲逛时，不确定、渴望、渴望取悦，人们似乎在看穿我们，目光聚焦在我们身后几码远的一些更真实的石头或树上。几乎没有人向我们打招呼；但也没有人皱眉或说任何令我们不愉快的话，这几乎同样令人满意。如果我们冒险接近某人（在这种气氛下，人们会强烈禁止这样做），他就会疏忽但明确地走开。如果他坐着或靠在墙上，我们把他困住了，他什么也不说，或者咕哝着，对巴厘岛人来说，这是终极的非字眼——“是的”。当然，这种冷漠是经过研究的。村民们注视着我们的一举一动，他们掌握了大量关于我们是谁以及我们要做什么的非常准确的信息。但他们的表现就好像我们根本不存在一样，事实上，这种行为的目的是告诉我们，我们不存在，或者无论如何还不存在。

blocks.en: This is, as I say, general in Bali. Everywhere else I have been in Indonesia, and more latterly in Morocco, when I have gone into a new village people have poured out from all sides to take a very close look at me, and, often, an all-tooprobing feel as well. In Balinese villages, at least those away from the tourist circuit, nothing happens at all. People go on pounding, chatting, making offerings, staring into space, carrying baskets about while one drifts around feeling vaguely disembodied. And the same thing is true on the individual level. When you first meet a Balinese, he seems virtually not to relate to you at all: he is, in the term Gregory Bateson and Margaret Mead made famous, “away.”1 Then–in a day, a week, a month (with some people the magic moment never comes)–he decides, for reasons I have never been quite able to fathom, that you are real, and then he becomes a warm, gay, sensitive, sympathetic, though, being Balinese, always precisely controlled person. You have crossed, somehow, some moral or metaphysical shadow line. Though you are not exactly taken as a Balinese (one has to be born to that), you are at least regarded as a human being rather than a cloud or a gust of wind. The whole complexion of your relationship dramatically changes to, in the majority of cases, a gentle, almost affectionate one–a low-keyed, rather playful, rather mannered, rather bemused geniality.
blocks.zh: 正如我所说，这是巴厘岛的普遍现象。我去过印度尼西亚的其他地方，最近又去过摩洛哥，当我走进一个新村庄时，人们从四面八方涌来，仔细地打量我，而且常常有一种令人生畏的感觉。在巴厘岛的村庄，至少是那些远离旅游线路的村庄，什么也没有发生。人们继续敲打、聊天、供奉、凝视太空、提着篮子到处走动，而人们却感觉模糊地脱离了实体。在个人层面上也是如此。当你第一次见到巴厘岛人时，他似乎与你根本没有任何关系：用格雷戈里·贝特森和玛格丽特·米德著名的术语来说，他是“离开”。1然后——在一天、一周、一个月（对某些人来说，神奇的时刻永远不会到来）——他决定，出于我一直无法理解的原因，你是真实的，然后他变成了一个热情、快乐、敏感、富有同情心的人，不过，作为巴厘岛人，总是受到严格控制的人。不知何故，你已经跨越了一些道德或形而上学的阴影线。虽然你不完全被视为巴厘岛人（必须是天生的），但你至少被视为一个人，而不是一朵云或一阵风。在大多数情况下，你们关系的整体面貌发生了巨大的变化，变成了一种温柔、近乎深情的关系——一种低调、相当有趣、相当有礼貌、相当困惑的友善。

blocks.en: My wife and I were still very much in the gust of wind stage, a most frustrating, and even, as you soon begin to doubt whether you are really real after all, unnerving one, when, ten days or so after our arrival, a large cockfight was held in the public square to raise money for a new school.
blocks.zh: 我和我的妻子还处于一阵风的阶段，这是一个最令人沮丧的阶段，甚至，当你很快开始怀疑自己是否真的真实时，甚至令人不安，在我们到达十天左右的时候，在公共广场上举行了一场大型斗鸡活动，为一所新学校筹集资金。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: Now, a few special occasions aside, cockfights are illegal in Bali under the Republic (as, for not altogether unrelated reasons, they were under the Dutch), largely as a result of the pretensions to puritanism radical nationalism tends to bring with it. The elite, which is not itself so very puritan, worries about the poor, ignorant peasant gambling all his money away, about what foreigners will think, about the waste of time better devoted to building up the country. It sees cockfighting as “primitive,” “backward,” “unprogressive,” and generally unbecoming an ambitious nation. And, as with those other embarrassments– opium smoking, begging, or uncovered breasts–it seeks, rather unsystematically, to put a stop to it.
blocks.zh: 现在，除了一些特殊场合之外，斗鸡在共和国统治下的巴厘岛是非法的（因为并非完全不相关的原因，斗鸡在荷兰统治下），很大程度上是由于激进民族主义往往会带来清教主义的结果。精英阶层本身并不是那么清教徒，他们担心贫穷无知的农民把所有的钱都赌光了，担心外国人会怎么想，担心浪费时间来建设国家。它认为斗鸡是“原始的”、“落后的”、“不进步的”，而且总体上不适合一个雄心勃勃的国家。而且，与其他令人尴尬的事情一样——吸鸦片、乞讨或裸露乳房——它试图以相当不系统的方式制止这种现象。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Of course, like drinking during Prohibition or, today, smoking marihuana, cockfights, being a part of “The Balinese Way of Life,” nonetheless go on happening, and with extraordinary frequency. And, like Prohibition or marihuana, from time to time the police (who, in 1958 at least, were almost all not Balinese but Javanese) feel called upon to make a raid, confiscate the cocks and spurs, fine a few people, and even now and then expose some of them in the tropical sun for a day as object lessons which never, somehow, get learned, even though occasionally, quite occasionally, the object dies.
blocks.zh: 当然，就像禁酒令期间的饮酒或今天吸食大麻一样，斗鸡作为“巴厘岛生活方式”的一部分，仍然继续发生，而且频率极高。而且，就像禁酒令或大麻一样，警察（至少在 1958 年，他们几乎都不是巴厘岛人，而是爪哇人）时不时地感到有必要进行一次突袭，没收雄鸡和马刺，对一些人处以罚款，甚至时不时地将其中一些在热带阳光下曝晒一天，作为实物教训，但无论如何，这些实物永远不会被吸取，尽管偶尔，非常偶然，该物体会死亡。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As a result, the fights are usually held in a secluded corner of a village in semisecrecy, a fact which tends to slow the action a little–not very much, but the Balinese do not care to have it slowed at all. In this case, however, perhaps because they were raising money for a school that the government was unable to give them, perhaps because raids had been few recently, perhaps, as I gathered from subsequent discussion, there was a notion that the necessary bribes had been paid, they thought they could take a chance on the central square and draw a larger and more enthusiastic crowd without attracting the attention of the law.
blocks.zh: 因此，战斗通常在村庄的一个僻静角落半秘密地进行，这一事实往往会稍微放慢行动速度，但巴厘人根本不介意放慢速度。然而，在这种情况下，也许是因为他们正在为一所政府无法提供给他们的学校筹集资金，也许是因为最近袭击很少，也许，正如我从随后的讨论中了解到的那样，有一种观念认为，必要的贿赂已经支付了，他们认为他们可以在中心广场上碰碰运气，吸引更多、更热情的人群，而不引起法律的注意。

blocks.en: On the established anthropological principle, When in Rome, my wife and I decided, only slightly less instantaneously than everyone else, that the thing to do was run too. We ran down the main village street, northward, away from where we were living, for we were on that side of the ring. About halfway down another fugitive ducked suddenly into a compound–his own, it turned out–and we, seeing nothing ahead of us but rice fields, open country, and a very high volcano, followed him. As the three of us came tumbling into the courtyard, his wife, who had apparently been through this sort of thing before, whipped out a table, a tablecloth, three chairs, and three cups of tea, and we all, without any explicit communication whatsoever, sat down, commenced to sip tea, and sought to compose ourselves.
blocks.zh: 根据既定的人类学原则，在罗马时，我和我的妻子决定，要做的事情也是跑步，只是比其他人稍微慢一点。我们沿着村庄的主要街道向北跑，远离我们住的地方，因为我们在环的那一侧。大约走到一半的时候，另一个逃亡者突然躲进一处院落——原来是他自己的院落——而我们，除了稻田、开阔的田野和一座很高的火山之外，什么也看不见，就跟在他后面。当我们三人跌跌撞撞地走进院子时，他的妻子显然以前经历过这种事情，拿出一张桌子、一块桌布、三把椅子和三杯茶，我们大家在没有任何明确的交流的情况下坐下来，开始喝茶，试图让自己平静下来。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: A few moments later, one of the policemen marched importantly into the yard, looking for the village chief. (The chief had not only been at the fight, he had arranged it. When the truck drove up he ran to the river, stripped off his sarong, and plunged in so he could say, when at length they found him sitting there pouring water over his head, that he had been away bathing when the whole affair had occurred and was ignorant of it. They did not believe him and fined him three hundred rupiah, which the village raised collectively.) Seeing my wife and I, “White Men,” there in the yard, the policeman performed a classic double take. When he found his voice again he asked, approximately, what in the devil did we think we were doing there. Our host of five minutes leaped instantly to our defense, producing an impassioned description of who and what we were, so detailed and so accurate that it was my turn, having barely communicated with a living human being save my landlord and the village chief for more than a week, to be astonished. We had a perfect right to be there, he said, looking the Javanese upstart in the eye. We were American professors; the government had cleared us; we were there to study culture; we were going to write a book to tell Americans about Bali. And we had all been there drinking tea and talking about cultural matters all afternoon and did not know anything about any cockfight. Moreover, we had not seen the village chief all day, he must have gone to town. The policeman retreated in rather total disarray. And, after a decent interval, bewildered but relieved to have survived and stayed out of jail, so did we.
blocks.zh: 过了一会儿，一名警察神气十足地走进院子，寻找村长。 （酋长不仅参加了战斗，而且还安排了这场战斗。当卡车开到河边时，他跑到河边，脱掉纱笼，跳进水里，以便他可以说，当最后他们发现他坐在那里，把水倒在头上时，他在整个事件发生时正在外面洗澡，对此一无所知。他们不相信他，并罚款他三百卢比，这是村里集体筹集的。）在那里看到我和我的妻子和我，“白人”，在那里在院子里，警察做了一个经典的双重观察。当他再次找到自己的声音时，他大致问道，我们到底以为我们在那里做什么。五分钟的主持人立刻站出来为我们辩护，对我们是谁、是什么进行了热情洋溢的描述，如此详细、如此准确，轮到我了，我在一个多星期的时间里几乎没有与除了房东和村长之外的活人交流过，我感到惊讶不已。我们完全有权利去那里，他看着这位爪哇新贵的眼睛说道。我们是美国教授；政府已经批准了我们；我们去那里是为了学习文化；我们打算写一本书来向美国人介绍巴厘岛。我们整个下午都在那里喝茶、谈论文化问题，对斗鸡一无所知。而且，我们一整天都没有见到村长，他一定是进城了。警察狼狈地撤退了。经过一段相当长的一段时间后，我们感到困惑，但又庆幸自己幸存下来并没有出狱，我们也是如此。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: The next morning the village was a completely different world for us. Not only were we no longer invisible, we were suddenly the center of all attention, the object of a great outpouring of warmth, interest, and, most especially, amusement. Everyone in the village knew we had fled like everyone else. They asked us about it again and again (I must have told the story, small detail by small detail, fifty times by the end of the day), gently, affectionately, but quite insistently teasing us: “Why didn’t you just stand there and tell the police who you were?” “Why didn’t you just say you were only watching and not betting?” “Were you really afraid of those little guns?” As always, kinesthetically minded and, even when fleeing for their lives (or, as happened eight years later, surrendering them), the world’s most poised people, they gleefully mimicked, also over and over again, our graceless style of running and what they claimed were our panic-stricken facial expressions. But above all, everyone was extremely pleased and even more surprised that we had not simply “pulled out our papers” (they knew about those too) and asserted our Distinguished Visitor status, but had instead demonstrated our solidarity with what were now our covillagers. (What we had actually demonstrated was our cowardice, but there is fellowship in that too.) Even the Brahmana priest, an old, grave, halfwayto-Heaven type who because of its associations with the underworld would never be involved, even distantly, in a cockfight, and was difficult to approach even to other Balinese, had us called into his courtyard to ask us about what had happened, chuckling happily at the sheer extraordinariness of it all.
blocks.zh: 第二天早上，这个村庄对我们来说是一个完全不同的世界。我们不仅不再是隐形的，而且突然成为所有人关注的中心，成为热情、兴趣、尤其是娱乐的对象。村里的每个人都知道我们和其他人一样逃走了。他们一次又一次地问我们这个问题（我肯定已经把这个故事一个个细节一个个细节地讲了，到一天结束时已经讲了五十遍了），温柔地、亲切地，但相当坚持地取笑我们：“你为什么不站在那里告诉警察你是谁？” “你为什么不直接说你只是看，不是赌？” “你真的害怕那些小枪吗？”一如既往，他们充满动觉，即使在逃命时（或者，八年后，他们投降了），他们是世界上最泰然自若的人，他们兴高采烈地模仿着我们粗鲁的奔跑风格，以及他们声称的我们惊慌失措的面部表情。但最重要的是，每个人都非常高兴，甚至更惊讶的是，我们不是简单地“拿出我们的文件”（他们也知道这些）并声称我们的尊贵访客身份，而是表明了我们与现在我们的村民的团结。 （我们实际上表现出的是我们的怯懦，但也有团契。）即使是婆罗门祭司，一个古老、严肃、半途而废的人，因为与地狱有联系，永远不会参与斗鸡，即使是遥远的，即使是其他巴厘人也很难接近，他也把我们叫到他的院子里，问我们发生了什么事，并为这一切的非凡而高兴地咯咯笑。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: In Bali, to be teased is to be accepted. It was the turning point so far as our relationship to the community was concerned, and we were quite literally “in.” The whole village opened up to us, probably more than it ever would have otherwise (I might actually never have gotten to that priest, and our accidental host became one of my best informants), and certainly very much faster. Getting caught, or almost caught, in a vice raid is perhaps not a very generalizable recipe for achieving that mysterious necessity of anthropological field work, rapport, but for me it worked very well. It led to a sudden and unusually complete acceptance into a society extremely difficult for outsiders to penetrate. It gave me the kind of immediate, inside-view grasp of an aspect of “peasant mentality” that anthropologists not fortunate enough to flee headlong with their subjects from armed authorities normally do not get. And, perhaps most important of all, for the other things might have come in other ways, it put me very quickly onto a combination emotional explosion, status war, and philosophical drama of central significance to the society whose inner nature I desired to understand. By the time I left I had spent about as much time looking into cockfights as into witchcraft, irrigation, caste, or marriage.
blocks.zh: 在巴厘岛，被嘲笑就是被接受。就我们与社区的关系而言，这是一个转折点，我们确实“融入”了。整个村庄向我们敞开心扉，可能比以往任何时候都更加开放（我实际上可能永远不会接触到那个牧师，而我们偶然的主人成为我最好的线人之一），而且当然要快得多。对于实现人类学田野工作的神秘必要性——融洽关系来说，在一次恶行袭击中被抓，或者几乎被抓，也许不是一个非常普遍的方法，但对我来说，它非常有效。它导致人们突然异常完全地接受了一个外人极难渗透的社会。它让我对“农民心态”的一个方面有一种直接的、内部的了解，而那些不幸带着他们的研究对象逃离武装当局的人类学家通常无法得到这种了解。也许最重要的是，因为其他事情可能以其他方式出现，它很快让我陷入了情感爆发、地位之争和对我渴望了解其内在本质的社会具有核心意义的哲学戏剧的结合。当我离开时，我花在研究斗鸡上的时间与研究巫术、灌溉、种姓或婚姻的时间差不多。

blocks.en: Bali, mainly because it is Bali, is a well-studied place. blocks.en: To anyone who has been in Bali any length of time, the deep psychological identification of Balinese men with their cocks is unmistakable. The double entendre here is deliberate. It works in exactly the same way in Balinese as it does in English, even to producing the same tired jokes, strained puns, and uninventive obscenities. Bateson and Mead have even suggested that, in line with the Balinese conception of the body as a set of separately animated parts, cocks are viewed as detachable, self-operating penises, ambulant genitals with a life of their own.4 And while I do not have the kind of unconscious material either to confirm or disconfirm this intriguing notion, the fact that they are masculine symbols par excellence is about as indubitable, and to the Balinese about as evident, as the fact that water runs downhill.
blocks.zh: 对于任何在巴厘岛呆过一段时间的人来说，巴厘岛男人对阴茎的深刻心理认同是显而易见的。这里的双关语是故意的。它在巴厘岛语中的运作方式与在英语中的运作方式完全相同，甚至会产生同样的乏味笑话、紧张的双关语和毫无创意的猥亵内容。贝特森和米德甚至提出，根据巴厘岛人将身体视为一组独立活动部分的概念，公鸡被视为可拆卸、自我操作的阴茎、具有自己生命的移动生殖器。 4虽然我没有那种无意识的材料来证实或反驳这个有趣的概念，但它们是卓越的男性象征这一事实是不容置疑的，对巴厘岛人来说正如水往低处流的事实一样显而易见。

blocks.en: The language of everyday moralism is shot through, on the male side of it, with roosterish imagery. Sabung, the word for cock (and one which appears in inscriptions as early as a.d. 922), is used metaphorically to mean “hero,” “warrior,” “champion,” “man of parts,” “political candidate,” “bachelor,” “dandy,” “ladykiller,” or “tough guy.” A pompous man whose behavior presumes above his station is compared to a tailless cock who struts about as though he had a large, spectacular one. A desperate man who makes a last, irrational effort to extricate himself from an impossible situation is likened to a dying cock who makes one final lunge at his tormentor to drag him along to a common destruction. A stingy man, who promises much, gives little, and begrudges that is compared to a cock which, held by the tail, leaps at another without in fact engaging him. A marriageable young man still shy with the opposite sex or someone in a new job anxious to make a good impression is called “a fighting cock caged for the first time.”5 Court trials, wars, political contests, inheritance disputes, and street arguments are all compared to cockfights.6 Even the very island itself is perceived from its shape as a small, proud cock, poised, neck extended, back taut, tail raised, in eternal challenge to large, feckless, shapeless Java.7

blocks.en: But the intimacy of men with their cocks is more than metaphorical. Balinese men, or anyway a large majority of Balinese men, spend an enormous amount of time with their favorites, grooming them, feeding them, discussing them, trying them out against one another, or just gazing at them with a mixture of rapt admiration and dreamy self-absorption. Whenever you see a group of Balinese men squatting idly in the council shed or along the road in their hips down, shoulders forward, knees up fashion, half or more of them will have a rooster in his hands, holding it between his thighs, bouncing it gently up and down to strengthen its legs, ruffling its feathers with abstract sensuality, pushing it out against a neighbor’s rooster to rouse its spirit, withdrawing it toward his loins to calm it again. blocks.zh: 但男人与鸡巴的亲密关系不仅仅是隐喻性的。巴厘岛男人，或者说大多数巴厘岛男人，会花大量的时间和他们最喜欢的人在一起，给他们梳理毛发，喂养他们，讨论他们，让他们互相较量，或者只是带着一种全神贯注的钦佩和梦幻般的自我陶醉的心情凝视着他们。每当你看到一群巴厘男人蹲在议会棚里或路边，臀部朝下，肩膀向前，膝盖向上，其中一半或更多的人手里会拿着一只公鸡，把它夹在大腿之间，轻轻地上下弹跳以加强它的腿，用抽象的性感来弄乱它的羽毛，将它推到邻居的公鸡上以唤醒它的精神，将它收回到腰部以使其平静。再次。有时，为了感受另一只鸟，男人会用这种方式摆弄别人的阴茎一段时间，但通常是走动蹲在它后面，而不是让它传给他，就好像它只是一只动物一样。

blocks.en: In the houseyard, the high-walled enclosures where the people live, fighting cocks are kept in wicker cages, moved frequently about so as to maintain the optimum balance of sun and shade. They are fed a special diet, which varies somewhat according to individual theories but which is mostly maize, sifted for impurities with far more care than it is when mere humans are going to eat it and offered to the animal kernel by kernel. Red pepper is stuffed down their beaks and up their anuses to give them spirit. They are bathed in the same ceremonial preparation of tepid water, medicinal herbs, flowers, and onions in which infants are bathed, and for a prize cock just about as often. Their combs are cropped, their plumage dressed, their spurs trimmed, their legs massaged, and they are inspected for flaws with the squinted concentration of a diamond merchant. A man who has a passion for cocks, an enthusiast in the literal sense of the term, can spend most of his life with them, and even those, the overwhelming majority, whose passion though intense has not entirely run away with them, can and do spend what seems not only to an outsider, but also to themselves, an inordinate amount of time with them. “I am cock crazy,” my landlord, a quite ordinary afficianado by Balinese standards, used to moan as he went to move another cage, give another bath, or conduct another feeding. “We’re all cock crazy.”
blocks.zh: 在人们居住的院子里，斗鸡被关在柳条笼子里，经常移动，以保持阳光和阴影的最佳平衡。它们被喂食一种特殊的饮食，根据个人的理论有所不同，但主要是玉米，比人类吃玉米时更加仔细地筛选杂质，然后将其逐粒提供给动物。红辣椒被塞进它们的喙和肛门，以给它们带来精神。他们沐浴在与婴儿沐浴相同的仪式准备中，包括温水、药草、鲜花和洋葱，对于获奖公鸡来说，沐浴的频率也差不多。他们的鸡冠被剪掉，他们的羽毛被修剪，他们的马刺被修剪，他们的腿被按摩，他们像钻石商人一样眯着眼睛专注地检查是否有瑕疵。一个对鸡巴充满热情的人，字面意义上的狂热者，可以与它们一起度过一生的大部分时间，甚至那些虽然热情强烈但并未完全消失的绝大多数人，可以而且确实花费了不仅在外人看来，而且在他们自己看来，与它们在一起的过多时间。 “我真是鸡鸡狂人”，我的房东，按照巴厘岛的标准，是个相当普通的爱好者，在搬另一个笼子、再洗一次澡或再一次喂食时常常抱怨道。 “我们都疯了。”

blocks.en: The madness has some less visible dimensions, however, because although it is true that cocks are symbolic expressions or magnifications of their owner’s self, the narcissistic male ego writ out in Aesopian terms, they are also expressions–and rather more immediate ones–of what the Balinese regard as the direct inversion, aesthetically, morally, and metaphysically, of human status: animality.
blocks.zh: 然而，这种疯狂还有一些不那么明显的维度，因为虽然公鸡确实是主人自我的象征性表达或放大，用伊索的术语写出自恋的男性自我，但它们也是巴厘人认为的人类地位的直接倒置（从美学上、道德上和形而上学上来说是动物性）的表达——而且是更直接的表达。

blocks.en: The Balinese revulsion against any behavior regarded as animal-like can hardly be overstressed. Babies are not allowed to crawl for that reason. Incest, though hardly approved, is a much less horrifying crime than bestiality. (The appropriate punishment for the second is death by drowning, for the first being forced to live like an animal.8) Most de-

blocks.en: The connection of cocks and cockfighting with such Powers, with the animalistic demons that threaten constantly to invade the small, cleared-off space in which the Balinese have so carefully built their lives and devour its inhabitants is quite explicit. A cockfight, any cockfight, is in the first instance a blood sacrifice offered, with the appropriate chants and oblations, to the demons in order to pacify their ravenous, cannibal hunger. No temple festival should be conducted until one is made. (If it is omitted someone will inevitably fall into a trance and command with the voice of an angered spirit that the oversight be immediately corrected.) Collective responses to natural evils–illness, crop failure, volcanic eruptions–almost always involve them. And that famous holiday in Bali, The Day of Silence (Njepi), when everyone sits silent and immobile all day long in order to avoid contact with a sudden influx of demons chased momentarily out of hell, is preceded the previous day by large-scale cockfights (in this case legal) in almost every village on the island.
blocks.zh: 公鸡和斗鸡与这些力量的联系，与不断威胁要入侵巴厘人小心翼翼地建立自己的生活并吞噬其居民的狭小而干净的空间的兽性恶魔的联系是相当明显的。斗鸡，任何斗鸡，首先都是用适当的圣歌和祭品向恶魔献上血祭，以平息他们食人般的饥饿。未定庙会，不得举办庙会。 （如果忽略了这一点，某人将不可避免地陷入恍惚状态，并用愤怒的灵魂的声音命令立即纠正疏忽。）对自然灾害——疾病、农作物歉收、火山爆发——的集体反应几乎总是涉及他们。巴厘岛著名的节日“沉默日”（Njepi），在这一天，每个人一整天都安静地坐着，一动不动，以避免与突然涌入的、暂时从地狱中被赶出来的恶魔接触。在前一天，岛上几乎每个村庄都会举行大规模斗鸡活动（在这种情况下是合法的）。

blocks.en: In the cockfight, man and beast, good and evil, ego and id, the creative power of aroused masculinity and the destructive power of loosened animality fuse in a bloody drama of hatred, cruelty, violence, and death. It is little wonder that when, as is the invariable rule, the owner of the winning cock takes the carcass of the loser–often torn limb from limb by its enraged owner–home to eat, he does so with a mixture of social embarrassment, moral satisfaction, aesthetic disgust, and cannibal joy. Or that a man who has lost an important fight is sometimes driven to wreck his family shrines and curse the gods, an act of metaphysical (and social) suicide. Or that in seeking earthly analogues for heaven and hell the Balinese compare the former to the mood of a man whose cock has just won, the latter to that of a man whose cock has just lost.
blocks.zh: 在斗鸡中，人与兽、善与恶、自我与本我、被唤醒的男子气概的创造力和放松的兽性的破坏力在一场充满仇恨、残忍、暴力和死亡的血腥戏剧中融合在一起。难怪，按照不变的规则，当获胜公鸡的主人把失败者的尸体——通常被愤怒的主人撕成碎片——带回家吃时，他带着社交尴尬、道德满足、审美厌恶和食人者的喜悦混合在一起。或者，一个在一场重要的战斗中失败的人有时会被迫破坏他的家庭神殿并诅咒众神，这是一种形而上学（和社会）自杀的行为。或者，在寻找天堂和地狱的尘世类比时，巴厘岛人将前者比作一个公鸡刚刚获胜的人的心情，将后者比作一个公鸡刚刚输了的人的心情。

blocks.en: Cockfights (tetadjen; sabungan) are held in a ring about fifty feet square. Usually they begin toward late afternoon and run three or four hours until sunset. About nine or ten separate matches (sehet) comprise a program. Each match is precisely like the others in general pattern: there is no main match, no connection between individual matches, no variation in their format, and each is arranged on a completely ad hoc basis. After a fight has ended and the emotional debris is cleaned away–the bets paid, the curses cursed, the carcasses possessed–seven, eight, perhaps even a dozen men slip negligently into the ring with a cock and seek to find there a logical opponent for it. This process, which rarely takes less than ten minutes, and often a good deal longer, is conducted in a very subdued, oblique, even dissembling manner. Those not immediately involved give it at best but disguised, sidelong attention; those who, embarrassedly, are, attempt to pretend somehow that the whole thing is not really happening.

blocks.en: A match made, the other hopefuls retire with the same deliberate indifference, and the selected cocks have their spurs (tadji) affixed–razor sharp, pointed steel swords, four or five inches long. This is a delicate job which only a small proportion of men, a half-dozen or so in most villages, know how to do properly. The man who attaches the spurs also provides them, and if the rooster he assists wins its owner awards him the spur-leg of the victim. The spurs are affixed by winding a long length of string around the foot of the spur and the leg of the cock. For reasons I shall come to presently, it is done somewhat differently from case to case, and is an obsessively deliberate affair. The lore about spurs is extensive–they are sharpened only at eclipses and the dark of the moon, should be kept out of the sight of women, and so forth. And they are handled, both in use and out, with the same curious combination of fussiness and sensuality the Balinese direct toward ritual objects generally.

blocks.en: The spurs affixed, the two cocks are placed by their handlers (who may or may not be their owners) facing one another in the center of the ring.9 A coconut pierced with a small hole is placed in a pail of water, in which it takes about twenty-one seconds to sink, a period known as a tjeng and marked at beginning and end by the beating of a slit gong. During these twenty-one seconds the handlers (pengangkeb) are not permitted to touch their roosters. If, as sometimes happens, the animals have not fought during this time, they are picked up, fluffed, pulled, prodded, and otherwise insulted, and put back in the center of the ring and the process begins again. Sometimes they refuse to fight at all, or one keeps running away, in which case they are imprisoned together under a wicker cage, which usually gets them engaged.

blocks.en: Most of the time, in any case, the cocks fly almost immediately at one another in a wing-beating, head-thrusting, leg-kicking explosion of animal fury so pure, so absolute, and in its own way so beautiful, as to be almost abstract, a Platonic concept of hate. Within moments one or the other drives home a solid blow with his spur. blocks.en: During this interval, slightly over two minutes, the handler of the wounded cock has been working frantically over it, like a trainer patching a mauled boxer between rounds, to get it in shape for a last, desperate try for victory. He blows in its mouth, putting the whole chicken head in his own mouth and sucking and blowing, fluffs it, stuffs its wounds with various sorts of medicines, and generally tries anything he can think of to arouse the last ounce of spirit which may be hidden somewhere within it. By the time he is forced to put it back down he is usually drenched in chicken blood, but, as in prizefighting, a good handler is worth his weight in gold. Some of them can virtually make the dead walk, at least long enough for the second and final round.

blocks.en: In the climactic battle (if there is one; sometimes the wounded cock simply expires in the handler’s hands or immediately as it is placed down again), the cock who landed the first blow usually proceeds to finish off his weakened opponent. But this is far from an inevitable outcome, for if a cock can walk he can fight, and if he can fight, he can kill, and what counts is which cock expires first. If the wounded one can get a stab in and stagger on until the other drops, he is the official winner, even if he himself topples over an instant later.
blocks.zh: 在激烈的战斗中（如果有的话；有时受伤的雄鸽会在训手手中死去，或者当它再次被放下时立即死去），首先击中的雄鸽通常会继续消灭他虚弱的对手。但这远非必然的结果，因为公鸡能走就可以打架，能打架就可以杀人，关键是哪只公鸡先死。如果受伤的一方能够被刺伤并摇摇晃晃地继续前进，直到另一方倒下，那么他就是正式的胜利者，即使他自己在一瞬间就倒下了。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: Surrounding all this melodrama– which the crowd packed tight around the ring follows in near silence, moving their bodies in kinesthetic sympathy with the movement of the animals, cheering their champions on with wordless hand motions, shiftings of the shoulders, turnings of the head, falling back en masse as the cock with the murderous spurs careens toward one side of the ring (it is said that spectators sometimes lose eyes and fingers from being too attentive), surging forward again as they glance off toward another–is a vast body of extraordinarily elaborate and precisely detailed rules.
blocks.zh: 围绕着这一切的情节剧——观众紧紧地围在赛场周围，几乎一片寂静，他们的身体随着动物的运动而移动，用无言的手势、肩膀的移动、头部的转动为他们的冠军欢呼，当公鸡带着凶残的马刺向赛场的一侧倾斜时，他们集体向后倒去(据说观众有时会因为太专心而失去眼睛和手指)，再次向前涌动，他们向另一个人瞥了一眼——这是一大堆非常复杂和精确的规则。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: These rules, together with the developed lore of cocks and cockfighting which accompanies them, are written down in palm-leaf manuscripts (lontar; rontal) passed on from generation to generation as part of the general legal and cultural tradition of the villages. At a fight, the umpire (saja komong; djuru kembar)–the man who manages the coconut–is in charge of their application and his authority is absolute. I have never seen an umpire’s judgment questioned on any subject, even by the more despondent losers, nor have I ever heard, even in private, a charge of unfairness directed against one, or, for that matter, complaints about umpires in general. Only exceptionally well-trusted, solid, and, given the complexity of the code, knowledgeable citizens perform this job, and in fact men will bring their cocks only to fights presided over by such men. It is also the umpire to whom accusations of cheating, which, though rare in the extreme, occasionally arise, are referred; and it is he who in the not infrequent cases where the cocks expire virtually together decides which (if either, for, though the Balinese do not care for such an outcome, there can be ties) went first. Likened to a judge, a king, a priest, and a policeman, he is all of these, and under his assured direction the animal passion of the fight proceeds within the civic certainty of the law. In the dozens of cockfights I saw in Bali, I never once saw an altercation about rules. Indeed, I never saw an open altercation, other than those between cocks, at all.
blocks.zh: 这些规则以及与之相伴的有关公鸡和斗鸡的发达知识，都记录在棕榈叶手稿（lontar；rontal）中，作为村庄一般法律和文化传统的一部分代代相传。在比赛中，裁判员（saja komong；djuru kembar）——管理椰子的人——负责其应用，他的权威是绝对的。我从未见过裁判员的判断在任何问题上受到质疑，即使是那些更加沮丧的失败者，也从未听到过，即使是私下里，针对某人的不公平指控，或者就此而言，对一般裁判员的抱怨。只有特别值得信赖、可靠且考虑到规则的复杂性、知识渊博的公民才能完成这项工作，事实上，男人只会带着他们的鸡巴参加由这样的男人主持的战斗。作弊指控也向裁判员提出，尽管这种情况极为罕见，但偶尔也会出现；在不少情况下，雄鸽几乎同时死去，都是由他来决定哪一只先行（如果有的话，尽管巴厘岛人不喜欢这样的结果，但可能会有平局）。与法官、国王、牧师和警察相比，他是所有这些人，在他确信的指导下，战斗的动物激情在法律的公民确定性范围内进行。在我在巴厘岛观看的数十场斗鸡比赛中，我从未见过因规则而发生争执。事实上，除了公鸡之间的争吵之外，我从未见过公开的争吵。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: This crosswise doubleness of an event which, taken as a fact of nature, is rage untrammeled and, taken as a fact of culture, is form perfected, defines the cockfight as a sociological entity. A cockfight is what, searching for a name for something not vertebrate enough to be called a group and not structureless enough to be called a crowd, Erving Goffman has called a “focused gathering”–a set of persons engrossed in a common flow of activity and relating to one another in terms of that flow.10 Such gatherings meet and disperse; the participants in them fluctuate; the activity that focuses them is discreet–a particulate process that reoccurs rather than a continuous one that endures. They take their form from the situation that evokes them, the floor on which they are placed, as Goffman puts it; but it is a form, and an articulate one, nonetheless. For the situation, the floor is itself created, in jury deliberations, surgical operations, block meetings, sit-ins, cockfights, by the cultural preoccupations–here, as we shall see, the celebration of status rivalry– which not only specify the focus but, assembling actors and arranging scenery, bring it actually into being.
blocks.zh: 一个事件的横向双重性，被视为自然事实，是不受约束的愤怒，而被视为文化事实，是形式完善的，将斗鸡定义为一个社会学实体。斗鸡就是为某种没有脊椎动物、不足以被称为群体、也没有无结构而被称为群体的东西寻找一个名称，欧文·戈夫曼称之为“集中的聚会”——一群全神贯注于共同的活动流程并在该流程中相互联系的人。10这样的聚会会相遇并散去；它们会聚集在一起，也会散开。参与者有波动；让他们集中注意力的活动是谨慎的——一个重复发生的微粒过程，而不是一个持久的连续过程。正如戈夫曼所说，它们的形式来自于唤起它们的情境，即它们所处的地板；但它仍然是一种形式，而且是一种清晰的形式。对于这种情况，场地本身是在陪审团审议、外科手术、集体会议、静坐、斗鸡等文化关注中创造出来的——正如我们将看到的，这里是对地位竞争的庆祝——它不仅明确了焦点，而且通过聚集演员和布置布景，使焦点真正成为现实。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In classical times (that is to say, prior to the Dutch invasion of 1908), when there were no bureaucrats around to improve popular morality, the staging of a cockfight was an explicitly societal matter. Bringing a cock to an important fight was, for an adult male, a compulsory duty of citizenship; taxation of fights, which were usually held on market day, was a major source of public revenue; patronage of the art was a stated responsibility of princes; and the cock ring, or wantilan, stood in the center of the village near those other monuments of Balinese civility–the council house, the origin temple, the marketplace, the signal tower, and the banyan tree. Today, a few special occasions aside, the newer rectitude makes so open a statement of the connection between the excitements of collective life and those of blood sport impossible, but, less directly expressed, the connection itself remains intimate and intact. To expose it, however, it is necessary to turn to the aspect of cockfighting around which all the others pivot, and through which they exercise their force, an aspect I have thus far studiously ignored. I mean, of course, the gambling.
blocks.zh: In classical times (that is to say, prior to the Dutch invasion of 1908) when there were no bureaucrats around to improve popular morality, the staging of a cockfight was an explicitly societal matter.对于成年男性来说，带公鸡参加重要的战斗是公民的一项强制性义务。通常在集市日举行的斗殴课税是公共收入的主要来源；赞助艺术是王子们的明确责任； and the cock ring, or wantilan, stood in the center of the village near those other monuments of Balinese civility-the council house, the origin temple, the marketplace, the signal tower, and the banyan tree. Today, a few special occasions aside, the newer rectitude makes so open a statement of the connection between the excitements of collective life and those of blood sport impossible, but, less directly expressed, the connection itself remains intimate and intact. To expose it, however, it is necessary to turn to the aspect of cockfighting around which all the others pivot, and through which they exercise their force, an aspect I have thus far studiously ignored.当然，我指的是赌博。

blocks.en: The Balinese never do anything in a simple way that they can contrive to do in a complicated one, and to this generalization cockfight wagering is no exception.
blocks.zh: 巴厘人从不以简单的方式做任何事情，他们可以设法用复杂的方式来做，对于这一概括，斗鸡投注也不例外。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: In the first place, there are two sorts of bets, or toh.11 There is the single axial bet
blocks.zh: 首先，有两种投注，或者 toh.11 有一种单轴投注
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The center bet is the official one, hedged in again with a webwork of rules, and is made between the two cock owners, with the umpire as overseer and public witness.12 This bet, which, as I say, is always relatively and sometimes very large, is never raised simply by the owner in whose name it is made, but by him together with four or five, sometimes seven or eight, allies–kin, village mates, neighbors, close friends. He may, if he is not especially well-to-do, not even be the major contributor, though, if only to show that he is not involved in any chicanery, he must be a significant one.
blocks.zh: 中心赌注是正式赌注，由规则网络进行对冲，由两个公鸡主人之间进行，裁判员作为监督者和公众见证人。 12正如我所说，这个赌注总是相对较大，有时很大，从来不是简单地由主人以其名义进行的，而是由他与四五个，有时是七八个，盟友亲戚，村友，邻居，亲密朋友一起提出。如果他不是特别富裕，他甚至可能不是主要贡献者，但是，如果只是为了表明他没有参与任何欺骗行为，他必须是一个重要的贡献者。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Of the 57 matches for which I have exact and reliable data on the center bet, the range is from 15 ringgits to 500, with a mean at 85 and with the distribution being rather noticeably trimodal: small fights (15 ringgits either side of 35) accounting for about 45 percent of the total number; medium ones (20 ringgits either side of 70) for about 25 percent; and large (75 ringgits either side of 175) for about 20 percent, with a few very small and very large ones out at the extremes. In a society where the normal daily wage of a manual laborer–a brickmaker, an ordinary farmworker, a market porter–was about 3 ringgits a day, and considering the fact that fights were held on the average about every 2.5 days in the immediate area I studied, this is clearly serious gambling, even if the bets are pooled rather than individual efforts.
blocks.zh: 在我掌握准确可靠的中注数据的 57 场比赛中，范围从 15 林吉特到 500 林吉特不等，平均为 85 林吉特，分布呈明显的三态：小规模斗殴（35 林吉特两边各 15 林吉特）约占总数的 45%；中型（70 林吉特两边各 20 林吉特）约占 25%；大型（175 林吉特左右各 75 林吉特）的比例约为 20%，极端情况下还有一些非常小和非常大的林吉特。在一个体力劳动者（砖匠、普通农场工人、市场搬运工）的正常日薪约为每天 3 林吉特的社会中，考虑到我所研究的邻近地区平均每 2.5 天就会发生一次打架斗殴事件，这显然是严重的赌博，即使赌注是集体赌注而不是个人努力。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The side bets are, however, something else altogether. Rather than the solemn, legalistic pactmaking of the center, wagering takes place rather in the fashion in which the stock exchange used to work when it was out on the curb. There is a fixed and known odds paradigm which runs in a continuous series from 10–9 at the short end to 2–1 at the long: 10–9, 9–8, 8–7, 7–6, 6–5, 5–4, 4–3, 3–2, 2–1. The man who wishes to back the underdog cock (leaving aside how favorites, kebut, and underdogs, ngai, are established for the moment) shouts the short-side number indicating the odds he wants to be given. That is, if he shouts gasal, “five,” he wants the underdog at 5–4 (or, for him, 4–5); if he shouts “four,” he wants it at 4–3 (again, he putting up the “three”), if “nine,” at 9–8, and so on. A man backing the favorite, and thus considering giving odds if he can get them short enough, indicates the fact by crying out the color type of that cock–“brown,” “speckled,” or whatever.13
blocks.zh: 然而，附带的赌注完全是另一回事。投注不是以中央庄严的、合法的契约方式进行的，而是以证券交易所在场外时的运作方式进行的。有一个固定且已知的赔率范例，从短盘的 10-9 到长盘的 2-1 连续排列：10-9、9-8、8-7、7-6、6-5、5-4、4-3、3-2、2-1。想要支持弱者公鸡的男子（暂时不考虑热门，kebut和弱者，ngai是如何建立的）喊出短边数字，表明他想要得到的赔率。也就是说，如果他喊加萨尔“五”，他希望失败者的比分是 5-4（或者，对他来说，是 4-5）；如果他喊“四”，他希望以 4-3 的比分（再次，他喊出“三”），如果他喊“九”，则以 9-8 的比分，依此类推。一个支持最喜欢的鸽子的男人，如果他能让它们足够短，就会考虑给出赔率，通过喊出那只公鸡的颜色类型——“棕色”、“斑点”或其他什么来表明这一事实。 13
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As odds-takers (backers of the underdog) and odds-givers (backers of the favorite) sweep the crowd with their shouts, they begin to focus in on one another as potential betting pairs, often from far across the ring. The taker tries to shout the giver into longer odds, the giver to shout the taker into shorter ones.14 The taker, who is the wooer in this situation, will signal how large a bet he wishes to make at the odds he is shouting by holding a number of fingers up in front of his face and vigorously waving them. If the giver, the wooed, replies in kind, the bet is made; if he does not, they unlock gazes and the search goes on.
blocks.zh: 当赔率接受者（弱者的支持者）和赔率提供者（热门球队的支持者）用他们的喊叫横扫人群时，他们开始关注彼此作为潜在的投注对，通常是从远离赛场的地方。接受者试图喊叫给予者更大的赔率，给予者则喊叫接受者更低的赔率。14在这种情况下，接受者（也就是求爱者）会通过将多根手指举在面前并用力挥舞来表示他希望按照他喊叫的赔率下多大的赌注。如果给予者、被追求者以同样的方式回应，则赌注成立；如果他不这样做，他们就会对视并继续搜索。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The side betting, which takes place after the center bet has been made and its size announced, consists then in a rising crescendo of shouts as backers of the underdog offer their propositions to anyone who will accept them, while those who are backing the favorite but do not like the price being offered, shout equally frenetically the color of the cock to show they too are desperate to bet but want shorter odds.
blocks.zh: 边注是在中心投注完成并宣布其大小之后进行的，包括当失败者的支持者向任何愿意接受他们的人提出他们的建议时，喊叫声不断上升，而那些支持热门但不喜欢所提供的价格的人，同样疯狂地喊出雄鸡的颜色，以表明他们也渴望下注，但想要更小的赔率。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Almost always odds-calling, which tends to be very consensual in that at any one time almost all callers are calling the same thing, starts off toward the long end of the range (5–4 or 4–3) and then moves, also consensually, toward the short end with greater or lesser speed and to a greater or lesser degree. Men crying “five” and finding themselves answered only with cries of “brown” start crying “six,” either drawing the other callers fairly quickly with them or retiring from the scene as their
blocks.zh: 几乎总是赔率跟注，这往往是非常一致的，因为在任何时候几乎所有跟注者都在叫同一件事，从范围的长端（5-4或4-3）开始，然后同样以或多或少的速度和或多或少的程度，一致地向短端移动。男人喊“五”，发现自己只得到“棕色”的呼喊，开始喊“六”，要么很快吸引其他呼叫者也跟着他们，要么退出现场，因为他们的
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As the moment for the release of the cocks by the handlers approaches, the screaming, at least in a match where the center bet is large, reaches almost frenzied proportions as the remaining unfulfilled bettors try desperately to find a last-minute partner at a price they can live with. (Where the center bet is small, the opposite tends to occur: betting dies off, trailing into silence, as odds lengthen and people lose interest.) In a largebet, well-made match–the kind of match the Balinese regard as “real cockfighting”–the mob scene quality, the sense that sheer chaos is about to break loose, with all those waving, shouting, pushing, clambering men is quite strong, an effect which is only heightened by the intense stillness that falls with instant suddenness, rather as if someone had turned off the current, when the slit gong sounds, the cocks are put down, and the battle begins.
blocks.zh: 随着训手放出雄鸽的时刻临近，至少在一场中心赌注很大的比赛中，尖叫声几乎达到了疯狂的程度，因为剩下的未完成的投注者拼命地试图以他们可以接受的价格找到最后一刻的合作伙伴。 （如果中心赌注很小，则往往会发生相反的情况：随着赔率增加，人们失去兴趣，赌注逐渐消失，陷入沉默。）在一场大赌注、精心制作的比赛中——巴厘岛人将这种比赛视为“真正的斗鸡”——暴徒场面质量，完全混乱即将爆发的感觉，所有那些挥手、喊叫、推搡、攀爬的人都非常强烈，这种效果只有在强烈的寂静中才会加剧。瞬间突然落下，就像有人关掉了电流一样，当缝锣一响，公鸡就放下了，战斗开始了。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: When it ends, anywhere from fifteen seconds to five minutes later, all bets are immediately paid. There are absolutely no ious, at least to a betting opponent. One may, of course, borrow from a friend before offering or accepting a wager, but to offer or accept it you must have the money already in hand and, if you lose, you must pay it on the spot, before the next match begins. This is an iron rule, and as I have never heard of a disputed umpire’s decision (though doubtless there must sometimes be some), I have also never heard of a welshed bet, perhaps because in a worked-up cockfight crowd the consequences might be, as they are reported to be sometimes for cheaters, drastic and immediate.
blocks.zh: 当比赛结束时，从十五秒到五分钟后，所有投注都会立即支付。绝对没有恶意，至少对于下注的对手来说是这样。当然，在提供或接受赌注之前，您可以向朋友借钱，但是要提供或接受赌注，您必须已经有钱在手，如果您输了，您必须在下一场比赛开始之前当场支付。这是一条铁律，而且我从未听说过有争议的裁判员的决定（尽管毫无疑问，有时肯定会有一些），我也从未听说过威尔士赌注，也许是因为在激动人心的斗鸡人群中，后果可能是激烈而直接的，正如据报道有时对作弊者来说。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It is, in any case, this formal asymmetry between balanced center bets and unbalanced side ones that poses the critical analytical problem for a theory which sees cockfight wagering as the link connecting the fight to the wider world of Balinese culture. It also suggests the way to go about solving it and demonstrating the link.
blocks.zh: 无论如何，平衡的中心赌注和不平衡的边赌注之间的这种形式上的不对称，给一种理论提出了关键的分析问题，该理论将斗鸡投注视为连接斗鸡与更广阔的巴厘岛文化世界的纽带。它还建议了解决该问题并演示链接的方法。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The first point that needs to be made in this connection is that the higher the center bet, the more likely the match will in actual fact be an even one. Simple considerations of rationality suggest that. If you are betting 15 ringgits on a cock, you might be willing to go along with even money even if you feel your animal somewhat the less promising. But if you are betting 500 you are very, very likely to be loathe to do so. Thus, in large-bet fights, which of course involve the better animals, tremendous care is taken to see that the cocks are about as evenly matched as to size, general condition, pugnacity, and so on as is humanly possible. The different ways of adjusting the spurs of the animals are often employed to secure this. If one cock seems stronger, an agreement will be made to position his spur at a slightly less advantageous angle–a kind of handicapping, at which spur affixers are, so it is said, extremely skilled. More care will be taken, too, to employ skillful handlers and to match them exactly as to abilities.
blocks.zh: 在这方面需要指出的第一点是，中心赌注越高，比赛实际上越有可能是平局。对理性的简单考虑表明了这一点。如果你在一只公鸡上赌 15 林吉特，即使你觉得你的动物不太有前途，你也可能愿意花甚至钱。但如果您下注 500，您可能非常非常不愿意这样做。因此，在大赌注的比赛中，当然涉及到更好的动物，我们会非常小心地确保雄鸽在体型、一般状况、好斗性等方面尽可能地匹配。通常采用不同的方法来调整动物的马刺来确保这一点。如果一只公鸡看起来更强壮，就会达成协议，将他的马刺放置在一个稍微不太有利的角度——这是一种障碍，据说，马刺固定者非常熟练。我们还将更加谨慎地聘用熟练的管理人员，并让他们与能力完全匹配。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In short, in a large-bet fight the pressure to make the match a genuinely fiftyfifty proposition is enormous, and is consciously felt as such. For medium fights the pressure is somewhat less, and for small ones less yet, though there is always an effort to make things at least approximately equal, for even at 15 ringgits (5 days’ work) no one wants to make an even-money bet in a clearly unfavorable situation. And, again, what statistics I have tend to bear this out. In my 57 matches, the favorite won 33 times overall, the underdog 24, a 1.4 to 1 ratio. But if one splits the figures at 60 ringgits center bets, the ratios turn out to be 1.1 to 1 (12 favorites, 11 underdogs) for those above this line, and 1.6 to 1 (21 and 13) for those below it. Or, if you take the extremes, for very large fights, those with center bets over 100 ringgits the ratio is 1 to 1 (7 and 7); for very small fights, those under 40 ringgits, it is 1.9 to 1 (19 and 10).16
blocks.zh: 简而言之，在一场大额赌注的战斗中，让比赛成为真正的五五十命题的压力是巨大的，并且是有意识地感受到的。对于中型比赛，压力要小一些，对于小型比赛，压力还小一些，尽管总是努力让事情至少大致相等，因为即使是 15 林吉特（5 天的工作），也没有人愿意在明显不利的情况下进行等额投注。再说一次，我所掌握的统计数据也证实了这一点。在我参加的 57 场比赛中，热门球队赢了 33 场，劣势球队赢了 24 场，比例为 1.4 比 1。但如果将数字分成 60 林吉特的中心赌注，则高于此线的比率为 1.1 比 1（12 个热门，11 个弱者），而低于此线的比率为 1.6 比 1（21 和 13）。或者，如果你采取极端的方式，对于非常大的战斗，那些中心赌注超过 100 林吉特的人，比率是 1 比 1（7 和 7）；对于非常小的战斗，即 40 林吉特以下的比赛，比例为 1.9 比 1（19 和 10）。16
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Now, from this proposition–that the higher the center bet the more exactly a fifty-fifty proposition the cockfight is– two things more or less immediately follow: (1) the higher the center bet, the greater is the pull on the side betting toward the short-odds end of the wagering spectrum and vice versa; (2) the higher the center bet, the greater the volume of side betting and vice versa.
blocks.zh: 现在，根据这个命题——中心赌注越高，斗鸡就越准确地是五五十命题——或多或少可以立即得出两件事：(1) 中心赌注越高，对投注范围的小赔率端的边注的吸引力就越大，反之亦然; (2) 中心投注额越高，边投注额越大，反之亦然。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The logic is similar in both cases. The closer the fight is in fact to even money, the less attractive the long end of the odds will appear and, therefore, the shorter it must be if there are to be takers. That this is the case is apparent from mere inspection, from the Balinese’s own analysis of the matter, and from what more systematic observations I was able to collect. Given the difficulty of making precise and complete recordings of side betting, this argument is hard to cast in numerical form, but in all my cases the odds-giver, odds-taker consensual point, a quite pronounced minimax saddle where the bulk (at a guess, two-thirds to three-quarters in most cases) of the bets are actually made, was three or four points further along the scale toward the shorter end
blocks.zh: 这两种情况的逻辑是相似的。事实上，比赛越接近平局，长赔率的吸引力就越小，因此，如果要有人接受，赔率就必须越短。仅从检查、巴厘岛人自己对此事的分析以及我能够收集到的更系统的观察来看，情况就是显而易见的。考虑到对边注进行精确和完整记录的难度，这个论点很难以数字形式表达，但在我的所有案例中，赔率提供者、赔率接受者的共识点，一个相当明显的极小极大鞍点，其中大部分（据猜测，大多数情况下是三分之二到四分之三）的投注实际上是在该点上进行的，沿着比例尺向较短的一端进一步移动了三到四个点
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The paradox of fair coin in the middle, biased coin on the outside is thus a merely apparent one. The two betting systems, though formally incongruent, are not really contradictory to one another, but part of a single larger system in which the center bet is, so to speak, the “center of gravity,” drawing, the larger it is the more so, the outside bets toward the short-odds end of the scale. The center bet thus “makes the game,” or perhaps better, defines it, signals what, following a notion of Jeremy Bentham’s, I am going to call its “depth.”
blocks.zh: 因此，“中间是公平的硬币，外面是有偏差的硬币”的悖论只是一个表面现象。这两个投注系统虽然形式上不一致，但实际上并不矛盾，而是一个更大系统的一部分，可以说，中心投注是“重心”，越大，外围投注越倾向于小赔率端。因此，中心赌注“创造了游戏”，或者更好地定义了游戏，标志着什么，按照杰里米·边沁的概念，我将称之为“深度”。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: The Balinese attempt to create an interesting, if you will, “deep,” match by making the center bet as large as possible so that the cocks matched will be as equal and as fine as possible, and the outcome, thus, as unpredictable as possible. They do not always succeed. Nearly half the matches are relatively trivial, relatively uninteresting–in my borrowed terminology, “shallow”–affairs. But that fact no more argues against my interpretation than the fact that most painters, poets, and playwrights are mediocre argues against the view that artistic effort is directed toward profundity and, with a certain frequency, approximates it. The image of artistic technique is indeed exact: the center bet is a means, a device, for creating “interesting,” “deep” matches, not the reason, or at least not the main reason, why they are interesting, the source of their fascination, the substance of their depth. The question why such matches are interesting–indeed, for the Balinese, exquisitely absorbing–takes us out of the realm of formal concerns into more broadly sociological and social-psychological ones, and to a less purely economic idea of what “depth” in gaming amounts to.18
blocks.zh: 巴厘岛人试图通过使中心赌注尽可能大来创造一场有趣的，如果你愿意的话，“深度”的比赛，这样匹配的雄鸽将尽可能平等和尽可能好，因此结果也尽可能不可预测。他们并不总是成功。近一半的比赛都是相对琐碎、相对无趣的——用我借用的术语来说，“肤浅”的事情。但这个事实并没有更多地反驳我的解释，就像大多数画家、诗人和剧作家都是平庸的事实反驳这样一种观点，即艺术的努力是指向深刻的，并且以一定的频率接近它。艺术技巧的形象确实是准确的：中心赌注是一种手段、一种装置，用于创造“有趣的”、“深刻的”匹配，而不是它们有趣的原因，或者至少不是主要原因，它们的魅力的源泉，它们的深度的实质。为什么这样的比赛很有趣——事实上，对于巴厘岛人来说，非常引人入胜——这个问题让我们脱离了正式关注的领域，进入了更广泛的社会学和社会心理学领域，以及对游戏“深度”意味着什么的不那么纯粹的经济概念。 18
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Bentham’s concept of “deep play” is found in his The Theory of Legislation.19 By it he means play in which the stakes are so high that it is, from his utilitarian standpoint, irrational for men to engage in it at all. If a man whose fortune is a thousand pounds (or ringgits) wages five hundred of it on an even bet, the marginal utility of the pound he stands to win is clearly less than the marginal disutility of the one he stands to lose. In genuine deep play, this is the case for both parties. They are both in over their heads. Having come together in search of pleasure they have entered into a relationship which will bring the participants, considered collectively, net pain rather than net pleasure. Bentham’s conclusion was, therefore, that deep play was immoral from first principles and, a typical step for him, should be prevented legally.
blocks.zh: 边沁的“深度游戏”概念可以在他的《立法理论》中找到。19他所说的“深度游戏”是指风险如此之高的游戏，从他的功利主义观点来看，人们参与其中根本不合理。如果一个拥有一千英镑（或林吉特）财富的人在平局中投注五百英镑，那么他赢得的英镑的边际效用显然小于他输掉的英镑的边际负效用。在真正的深度比赛中，双方都是如此。他们都难以应对。为了寻找快乐而走到一起，他们建立了一种关系，这种关系将给参与者带来净痛苦，而不是净快乐。因此，边沁的结论是，深度游戏从首要原则来看是不道德的，对他来说这是一个典型的步骤，应该从法律上加以阻止。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: But more interesting than the ethical problem, at least for our concerns here, is that despite the logical force of Bentham’s analysis men do engage in such play, both passionately and often, and even in the face of law’s revenge. For Bentham and those who think as he does (nowadays mainly lawyers, economists, and a few psychiatrists), the explanation is, as I have said, that such men are irrational–addicts, fetishists, children, fools, savages, who need only to be protected against themselves. But for the Balinese, though naturally they do not formulate it in so many words, the explanation lies in the fact that in such play money is less a measure of utility, had or expected, than it is a symbol of moral import, perceived or imposed.
blocks.zh: 但比道德问题更有趣的是，至少就我们在这里的担忧而言，尽管边沁的分析具有逻辑力量，但人们确实热衷于经常参与这种游戏，甚至面对法律的报复。对于边沁和那些与他想法相同的人（现在主要是律师、经济学家和一些精神病学家）来说，解释是，正如我所说的，这些人是非理性的——瘾君子、恋物癖者、儿童、傻瓜、野蛮人，他们只需要受到保护以免受他们自己的伤害。但对于巴厘岛人来说，虽然他们自然不会用那么多的词语来表达它，但解释在于这样一个事实：在这种游戏中，货币与其说是一种已有的或预期的效用的衡量标准，不如说它是一种道德意义的象征，无论是感知的还是强加的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It is, in fact, in shallow games, ones in which smaller amounts of money are involved, that increments and decrements of cash are more nearly synonyms for utility and disutility, in the ordinary, unexpanded sense–for pleasure and pain, happiness and unhappiness. In deep ones, where the amounts of money are great, much more is at stake than material gain: namely, esteem, honor, dignity, respect–in a word, though in Bali a profoundly freighted word, status.20 It is at stake symbolical-
blocks.zh: 事实上，在涉及较少金额的浅层游戏中，现金的增加和减少更接近于普通的、未扩展的意义上的效用和负效用的同义词——快乐和痛苦、幸福和不幸福。在金钱数额巨大的深层关系中，比物质利益更重要的是：即尊重、荣誉、尊严、尊重——总而言之，尽管在巴厘岛，地位是一个意义深远的词。20它具有象征意义——
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: This, I must stress immediately, is not to say that the money does not matter, or that the Balinese is no more concerned about losing 500 ringgits than 15. Such a conclusion would be absurd. It is because money does, in this hardly unmaterialistic society, matter and matter very much that the more of it one risks the more of a lot of other things, such as one’s pride, one’s poise, one’s dispassion, one’s masculinity, one also risks, again only momentarily but again very publicly as well. In deep cockfights an owner and his collaborators, and, as we shall see, to a lesser but still quite real extent also their backers on the outside, put their money where their status is.
blocks.zh: 我必须立即强调，这并不是说钱不重要，或者巴厘岛人对失去 500 林吉特并不比失去 15 林吉特更关心。这样的结论是荒谬的。正是因为金钱在这个几乎非物质主义的社会里确实非常重要，所以一个人所冒的风险越多，其他很多东西的风险就越大，比如一个人的骄傲、一个人的镇定、一个人的冷静、一个人的男子气概，一个人也会冒风险，同样只是暂时的，但也是非常公开的。在深入的斗鸡中，斗鸡的主人和他的合作者，以及我们将看到的，在较小但仍然相当真实的程度上，还有他们的外部支持者，将他们的钱花在了他们的地位上。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It is in large part because the marginal disutility of loss is so great at the higher levels of betting that to engage in such betting is to lay one’s public self, allusively and metaphorically, through the medium of one’s cock, on the line. And though to a Benthamite this might seem merely to increase the irrationality of the enterprise that much further, to the Balinese what it mainly increases is the meaningfulness of it all. And as (to follow Weber rather than Bentham) the imposition of meaning on life is the major end and primary condition of human existence, that access of significance more than compensates for the economic costs involved.21 Actually, given the even-money quality of the larger matches, important changes in material fortune among those who regularly participate in them seem virtually nonexistent, because matters more or less even out over the long run. It is, actually, in the smaller, shallow fights, where one finds the handful of more pure, addict-type gamblers involved–those who are in it mainly for the money–that “real” changes in social position, largely downward, are affected. Men of this sort, plungers, are highly dispraised by “true cockfighters” as fools who do not understand what the sport is all about, vulgarians who simply miss the point of it all. They are, these addicts, regarded as fair game for the genuine enthusiasts, those who do understand, to take a little money away from, something that is easy enough to do by luring them, through the force of their greed, into irrational bets on mismatched cocks. Most of them do indeed manage to ruin themselves in a remarkably short time, but there always seems to be one or two of them around, pawning their land and selling their clothes in order to bet, at any particular time.22
blocks.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为在较高水平的投注中，损失的边际负效用是如此之大，以至于从事这种投注就是通过暗示和隐喻的方式，通过一个人的鸡巴将一个人的公共自我置于赌注之上。尽管对边沁主义者来说，这似乎只是进一步增加了企业的非理性，但对巴厘岛人来说，它主要增加的是这一切的意义。而且（按照韦伯的说法，而不是边沁的说法），赋予生命意义是人类存在的主要目的和首要条件，获得意义的意义远远超过了所涉及的经济成本的补偿。21实际上，考虑到大型比赛的均等金钱质量，经常参加比赛的人的物质财富的重大变化似乎几乎不存在，因为从长远来看，这些变化或多或少都是平等的。事实上，正是在规模较小、浅薄的斗殴中，人们发现少数更纯粹、上瘾的赌徒参与其中——那些主要是为了钱而参与其中的人——社会地位的“真正”变化（很大程度上是下降的）受到影响。这类人，即柱塞人，被“真正的斗鸡士”高度评价为不了解这项运动的全部内容的傻瓜，以及根本没有抓住要点的庸人。他们，这些瘾君子，被认为是真正的爱好者的公平游戏，那些真正理解的人，可以从中拿走一点钱，通过他们的贪婪的力量，引诱他们对不匹配的公鸡进行非理性的赌注，这是很容易做到的。他们中的大多数人确实在极短的时间内毁掉了自己，但似乎总有那么一两个人在任何特定的时间典当他们的土地并出售他们的衣服以进行赌博。 22
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: This graduated correlation of “status gambling” with deeper fights and, inversely, “money gambling” with shallower ones is in fact quite general. Bettors themselves form a sociomoral hierarchy in these terms. As noted earlier, at most cockfights there are, around the very edges of the cockfight area, a large number of mindless, sheer-chance type gambling games (roulette, dice throw, coin-spin, pea-under-the-shell) operated by concessionaires. Only women, children, adolescents, and various other sorts of people who do not (or not yet) fight cocks–the extremely poor, the socially despised, the personally idiosyncratic–play at these games, at, of course, penny ante levels. Cockfighting men would be ashamed to go anywhere near them. Slightly above these people in standing are those who, though they do not themselves fight cocks, bet on the smaller matches around the edges. Next, there are those who fight cocks in small, or occasionally medium matches, but have not the status to join in the large ones, though they may bet from time to time on the side in those. And finally, there are those, the really substantial members of the community, the solid citizenry around whom local life revolves, who fight in the larger fights and bet on them around the side. The focusing element in these focused gatherings, these men generally dominate and define the sport as they dominate and define the society. When a Balinese male talks, in that almost venerative way, about “the true cockfighter,” the bebatoh (“bettor”) or djuru kurung (“cage keeper”), it is this sort of person, not those who bring the mentality of the pea-and-shell game into the quite different, inappropriate context of the cockfight, the driven gambler (potét, a word which has the secondary meaning of thief or reprobate), and the wistful hanger-on, that they mean. For such a man, what is really going on in a match is something rather closer to an affaire d’honneur (though, with the Balinese talent for practical fantasy, the blood that is spilled is only figuratively human) than to the stupid, mechanical crank of a slot machine.
blocks.zh: “地位赌博”与更深层次的争斗以及相反的“金钱赌博”与较浅层次的争斗的这种渐进相关性实际上是相当普遍的。从这些角度来看，博彩者本身就形成了社会道德等级制度。如前所述，在大多数斗鸡活动中，在斗鸡区域的边缘，都有大量由特许经营者经营的无意识的、纯粹碰运气的赌博游戏（轮盘赌、掷骰子、转硬币、壳下豌豆）。只有妇女、儿童、青少年和其他各种不（或尚未）斗鸡的人——赤贫者、社会鄙视者、个人特质——玩这些游戏，当然，赌注水平很低。斗鸡的人会羞于靠近它们。地位稍高于这些人的是那些虽然自己不斗鸡但在边缘较小的比赛上下注的人。其次，还有一些人在小型比赛中斗鸡，或者偶尔在中型比赛中斗鸡，但没有资格参加大型比赛，尽管他们可能偶尔会在这些比赛中下注。最后，还有一些人，社区中真正重要的成员，当地生活围绕着他们的坚实公民，他们参加更大的战斗，并在他们周围下注。这些男性是这些集中聚会中的焦点元素，他们通常主导和定义这项运动，就像他们主导和定义社会一样。当巴厘岛男性以一种近乎崇敬的方式谈论“真正的斗鸡”、bebatoh（“赌徒”）或 djuru kurung（“笼子饲养员”）时，他就是这类人，而不是那些将豌豆和贝壳游戏的心态带入完全不同的、不恰当的斗鸡背景中的人，即被驱使的赌徒（potét，这个词具有小偷或小偷的次要含义）。被遗弃者），他们指的是渴望的食客。对于这样一个人来说，比赛中真正发生的事情更接近于一场荣誉事件（尽管巴厘岛人具有实际幻想的天赋，所流的鲜血只是象征性的人类）而不是老虎机上愚蠢的机械曲柄。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: What makes Balinese cockfighting deep is thus not money in itself, but what, the more of it that is involved the more so, money causes to happen: the migration of the Balinese status hierarchy into the body of the cockfight. Psychologically an Aesopian representation of the ideal/demonic, rather narcissistic, male self, sociologically it is an equally Aesopian representation of the complex fields of tension set up by the controlled, muted, ceremonial, but for all that deeply felt, interaction of those selves in the context of everyday life.
