blocks.en: The easiest way to make this clear, and at least to some degree to demonstrate it, is to invoke the village whose cockfighting activities I observed the closest–the one in which the raid occurred and from which my statistical data are taken.
blocks.zh: 要阐明这一点，至少在某种程度上证明这一点，最简单的方法是援引我观察到最接近的斗鸡活动的村庄——袭击发生的那个村庄，我的统计数据就是从那个村庄获取的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As all Balinese villages, this one– Tihingan, in the Klungkung region of southeast Bali–is intricately organized, a labyrinth of alliances and oppositions. But, unlike many, two sorts of corporate groups, which are also status groups, particularly stand out, and we may concentrate on them, in a part-for-whole way, without undue distortion.
blocks.zh: 与所有巴厘岛村庄一样，这个位于巴厘岛东南部 Klungkung 地区的 Tihingan 村庄组织错综复杂，是一个联盟和反对派的迷宫。但是，与许多企业集团不同的是，有两种同样是地位群体的企业集团特别引人注目，我们可以以部分为整体的方式关注它们，而不会过度扭曲。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: First, the village is dominated by four large, patrilineal, partly endogamous descent groups which are constantly vying with one another and form the major factions in the village. Sometimes they group two and two, or rather the two larger ones versus the two smaller ones plus all the unaffiliated people; sometimes they operate independently. There are also subfactions within them, subfactions within the subfactions, and so on to rather fine levels of distinction. And second, there is the village itself, almost entirely endogamous, which is opposed to all the other villages round about in its cockfight circuit (which, as explained, is the market region), but which also forms alliances with certain of these neighbors against certain others in various supravillage political and social contexts. The exact situation is thus, as everywhere in Bali, quite distinctive; but the general pattern of a tiered hierarchy of status rivalries between highly corporate but various based groupings (and, thus, between the members of them) is entirely general.
blocks.zh: 首先，该村由四个大的、父系的、部分同族通婚的后裔群体所主导，这些群体不断相互竞争，形成了村里的主要派系。有时他们两个两个一组，或者更确切地说，两个较大的人与两个较小的人加上所有无关的人；有时他们独立运作。它们内部还存在子派系，子派系内还有子派系，等等，以至相当精细的区分级别。其次，是村庄本身，几乎完全是同族通婚，它与斗鸡场周围的所有其他村庄相对立（正如所解释的，这是市场区域），但它也与这些邻居中的某些邻居结成联盟，在各种超村庄政治和社会背景下对抗某些其他村庄。因此，正如巴厘岛的其他地方一样，确切的情况是非常独特的。但是，高度企业化但基础不同的团体之间（以及这些团体的成员之间）地位竞争的分层等级制度的一般模式是完全普遍的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Consider, then, as support of the general thesis that the cockfight, and especially the deep cockfight, is fundamentally a dramatization of status concerns, the following facts, which to avoid extended ethnographic description I will simply pronounce to be facts–though the concrete evidence-examples, statements, and numbers that could be brought to bear in support of them is both extensive and unmistakable:
blocks.zh: 那么，考虑一下，作为对斗鸡，尤其是深度斗鸡，从根本上来说是地位问题的戏剧化这一一般论点的支持，以下事实，为了避免扩展的民族志描述，我将简单地宣布它们是事实——尽管可以用来支持它们的具体证据——例子、陈述和数字既广泛又明确无误：
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 1. A man virtually never bets against a cock owned by a member of his own kingroup. Usually he will feel obliged to bet for it, the more so the closer the kin tie and the deeper the fight. If he is certain
blocks.zh: 1. 一个人实际上从不打赌自己亲属拥有的公鸡。通常，他会觉得有必要为此下注，而且血缘关系越密切，争斗越激烈，他就越是如此。如果他确定的话
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: in his mind that it will not win, he may just not bet at all, particularly if it is only a second cousin’s bird or if the fight is a shallow one. But as a rule he will feel he must support it and, in deep games, nearly always does. Thus the great majority of the people calling “five” or “speckled” so demonstratively are expressing their allegiance to their kinsman, not their evaluation of his bird, their understanding of probability theory, or even their hopes of unearned income.
blocks.zh: 如果他认为这只鸽子不会赢，他可能根本就不打赌，特别是如果这只鸽子只是二表弟的鸽子，或者比赛很浅的话。但通常来说，他会觉得自己必须支持它，而且在深度比赛中，几乎总是如此。因此，绝大多数人如此明确地称呼“五”或“斑点”是在表达他们对亲戚的忠诚，而不是他们对他的鸟的评价，他们对概率论的理解，甚至他们对不劳而获的收入的希望。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 2. This principle is extended logically. If your kingroup is not involved you will support an allied kingroup against an unallied one in the same way, and so on through the very involved networks of alliances which, as I say, make up this, as any other, Balinese village.
blocks.zh: 2. 这一原则得到了逻辑上的扩展。如果你的亲属团体没有参与其中，你将以同样的方式支持一个结盟的亲属团体对抗一个不结盟的亲属团体，等等，通过非常复杂的联盟网络，正如我所说，这些联盟网络构成了这个，就像任何其他巴厘岛村庄一样。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 3. So, too, for the village as a whole. If an outsider cock is fighting any cock from your village you will tend to support the local one. If, what is a rarer circumstance but occurs every now and then, a cock from outside your cockfight circuit is fighting one inside it you will also tend to support the “home bird.”
blocks.zh: 3. 对于整个村庄来说也是如此。如果一只外地公鸡与你村里的任何一只公鸡战斗，你会倾向于支持本地公鸡。如果，一种比较罕见但时常发生的情况，一只来自斗鸡场外的公鸡正在与场内的另一只公鸡打斗，你也会倾向于支持“家鸟”。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 4. Cocks which come from any distance are almost always favorites, for the theory is the man would not have dared to bring it if it was not a good cock, the more so the further he has come. His followers are, of course, obliged to support him, and when the more grand-scale legal cockfights are held (on holidays, and so on) the people of the village take what they regard to be the best cocks in the village, regardless of ownership, and go off to support them, although they will almost certainly have to give odds on them and to make large bets to show that they are not a cheapskate village. Actually, such “away games,” though infrequent, tend to mend the ruptures between village members that the constantly occurring “home games,” where
blocks.zh: 4.来自任何距离的雄鸡几乎总是最受欢迎的，因为理论上来说，如果不是好雄鸡，男人就不敢带它，而且他来得越远，就越不敢带它来。当然，他的追随者有义务支持他，当举行更大规模的合法斗鸡活动时（节假日等），村里的人会挑选他们认为是村里最好的公鸡，不管所有权如何，然后去支持它们，尽管他们几乎肯定要给它们下注，并下大赌注，以表明他们不是一个小气的村庄。事实上，这种“客场比赛”虽然不常见，但往往比不断发生的“主场比赛”更能弥合村民之间的裂痕。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: village factions are opposed rather than united, exacerbate.
blocks.zh: 村里各派非但不团结，相互对立，愈演愈烈。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 5. Almost all matches are sociologically relevant. You seldom get two outsider cocks fighting, or two cocks with no particular group backing, or with group backing which is mutually unrelated in any clear way. When you do get them, the game is very shallow, betting very slow, and the whole thing very dull, with no one save the immediate principals and an addict gambler or two at all interested.
blocks.zh: 5. 几乎所有匹配都具有社会学相关性。你很少会看到两只外来的公鸡打架，或者两只没有特定群体支持的公鸡打架，或者得到的群体支持在任何明显的方式上都没有相互关联。当你真正得到它们时，游戏非常浅薄，下注非常缓慢，整个事情非常乏味，除了直接的校长和一两个上瘾的赌徒之外没有人感兴趣。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 6. By the same token, you rarely get two cocks from the same group, even more rarely from the same subfaction, and virtually never from the same sub-subfaction (which would be in most cases one extended family) fighting. Similarly, in outside village fights two members of the village will rarely fight against one another, even though, as bitter rivals, they would do so with enthusiasm on their home grounds.
blocks.zh: 6. 出于同样的原因，你很少会看到两只来自同一群体的雄鸽，更罕见的是来自同一亚派系的雄鸽，而且几乎从来不会来自同一亚亚派系（在大多数情况下是一个大家庭）的斗鸡。同样，在村外打架时，两个村里的人很少会互相打斗，尽管作为死对头，他们会在自己的土地上热情地这样做。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 7. On the individual level, people involved in an institutionalized hostility relationship, called puik, in which they do not speak or otherwise have anything to do with each other (the causes of this formal breaking of relations are many: wife-capture, inheritance arguments, political differences) will bet very heavily, sometimes almost maniacally, against one another in what is a frank and direct attack on the very masculinity, the ultimate ground of his status, of the opponent.
blocks.zh: 7. 在个人层面上，陷入一种制度化的敌对关系（称为“puik”）的人们，在这种关系中，他们彼此之间不说话或没有任何关系（这种正式关系破裂的原因有很多：夺妻、遗产争论、政治分歧），他们会非常激烈地、有时甚至近乎疯狂地相互下注，坦率而直接地攻击对手的男子气概，即他的地位的最终基础。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 8. The center bet coalition is, in all but the shallowest games, always made up by structural allies–no “outside money” is involved. What is “outside” depends upon the context, of course, but given it, no outside money is mixed in with the main bet; if the principals cannot raise it, it is not made. The center bet, again especially in deeper games, is thus the most direct and open expression of social opposition,
blocks.zh: 8. 除了最浅的游戏外，中心投注联盟总是由结构性盟友组成——不涉及“外部资金”。当然，什么是“外部”取决于具体情况，但考虑到这一点，主要赌注中不会混入外部资金；如果校长不能提出，就不会制定。因此，中心赌注，特别是在更深层次的游戏中，是社会反对最直接和公开的表达，
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 9. The rule about borrowing money– that you may borrow for a bet but not in one–stems (and the Balinese are quite conscious of this) from similar considerations: you are never at the economic mercy of your enemy that way. Gambling debts, which can get quite large on a rather short-term basis, are always to friends, never to enemies, structurally speaking.
blocks.zh: 9. 关于借钱的规则——你可以借钱打赌，但不能借钱——源于类似的考虑（巴厘岛人很清楚这一点）：这样你就永远不会受到敌人的经济摆布。从结构上讲，赌博债务在相当短的时间内可能会变得相当大，这些债务总是属于朋友，而不是敌人。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 10. When two cocks are structurally irrelevant or neutral so far as you are concerned (though, as mentioned, they almost never are to each other) you do not even ask a relative or a friend whom he is betting on, because if you know how he is betting and he knows you know, and you go the other way, it will lead to strain. This rule is explicit and rigid; fairly elaborate, even rather artificial precautions are taken to avoid breaking it. At the very least you must pretend not to notice what he is doing, and he what you are doing.
blocks.zh: 10. 当两只公鸡在结构上对你来说是不相关或中立的（尽管，正如前面提到的，它们几乎从不相互相关），你甚至不会问他的亲戚或朋友他在谁身上下注，因为如果你知道他如何下注并且他知道你知道，而你却走另一条路，就会导致紧张。这个规则是明确的、严格的；为了避免破坏它，采取了相当复杂的、甚至是人为的预防措施。至少你必须假装没有注意到他在做什么，以及他在做什么。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 11. There is a special word for betting against the grain, which is also the word for “pardon me” (mpura). It is considered a bad thing to do, though if the center bet is small it is sometimes all right as long as you do not do it too often. But the larger the bet and the more frequently you do it, the more the “pardon me” tack will lead to social disruption.
blocks.zh: 11. 有一个特殊的词来表示对赌，这也是“请原谅我”（mpura）的词。这被认为是一件坏事，但如果中心赌注很小，有时只要你不经常这样做就可以。但赌注越大，赌注越频繁，“请原谅我”策略就越会导致社会混乱。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 12. In fact, the institutionalized hostility relation, puik, is often formally initiated (though its causes always lie elsewhere) by such a “pardon me” bet in a deep fight, putting the symbolic fat in the fire. Similarly, the end of such a relationship and resumption of normal social intercourse is often signalized (but, again, not actually brought about) by one or the other of the enemies supporting the other’s bird.
blocks.zh: 12. 事实上，制度化的敌对关系（puik）常常是通过在一场激烈的战斗中进行“请原谅我”的赌注而正式引发的（尽管其原因总是在其他地方），将象征性的脂肪投入火中。同样，这种关系的结束和正常社会交往的恢复通常是由敌人中的一个或另一个支持对方的鸟来表示的（但同样，这并不是真正发生的）。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 13. In sticky, cross-loyalty situations, of which in this extraordinarily complex social system there are of course many, where a man is caught between two more or less equally balanced loyalties, he tends to wander off for a cup of coffee or something to avoid having to bet, a form of behavior reminiscent of that of American voters in similar situations.25
blocks.zh: 13. 在这种极其复杂的社会体系中，这种情况当然有很多，当一个人陷入两种或多或少平衡的忠诚之间时，他往往会走开去喝杯咖啡或其他东西，以避免必须下注，这种行为让人想起美国选民在类似情况下的行为。 25
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 14. The people involved in the center bet are, especially in deep fights, virtually always leading members of their group– kinship, village, or whatever. Further, those who bet on the side (including these people) are, as I have already remarked, the more established members of the village–the solid citizens. Cockfighting is for those who are involved in the everyday politics of prestige as well, not for youth, women, subordinates, and so forth.
blocks.zh: 14. 参与中心赌注的人，尤其是在激烈的战斗中，实际上总是领导着他们的团体（亲属、村庄或其他团体）的成员。此外，正如我已经说过的，那些旁观者（包括这些人）是村里更有地位的成员——可靠的公民。斗鸡也适合那些参与日常声望政治的人，而不适合年轻人、妇女、下属等。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 15. So far as money is concerned, the explicitly expressed attitude toward it is that it is a secondary matter. It is not, as I have said, of no importance; Balinese are no happier to lose several weeks’ income than anyone else. But they mainly look on the monetary aspects of the cockfight as self-balancing, a matter of just moving money around, circulating it among a fairly well-defined group of serious cockfighters. The really important wins and losses are seen mostly in other terms, and the general attitude toward wagering is not any hope of cleaning up, of making a killing (addict gamblers again excepted), but that of the horseplayer’s prayer: “Oh, God, please let me break even.” In prestige terms, however, you do not want to break even, but, in a momentary, punctuate sort of way, win utterly. The talk (which goes on all the time) is about fights against such-and-such a cock of So-and-So which
blocks.zh: 15. 就金钱而言，明确表达的态度是，它是次要的。正如我所说，这并非不重要；而是重要的。巴厘岛人对于失去几周的收入并不比其他人更高兴。但他们主要认为斗鸡的金钱方面是自我平衡的，只是转移金钱，在一群相当明确的严肃斗鸡者中流通。真正重要的输赢大多是从其他角度来看待的，人们对下注的普遍态度并不是希望能够干净利落、大赚一笔（赌徒上瘾的人除外），而是赌马者的祈祷：“哦，上帝，请让我收支平衡。”然而，就声望而言，你不想收支平衡，而是想以一种短暂的、间断的方式彻底获胜。谈话（一直在进行）是关于与某某公鸡的战斗，
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: your cock demolished, not on how much you won, a fact people, even for large bets, rarely remember for any length of time, though they will remember the day they did in Pan Loh’s finest cock for years.
blocks.zh: 你的鸡鸡被摧毁了，而不是你赢了多少，这一事实人们，即使是大赌注，也很少会记住很长一段时间，尽管他们会记得他们在潘洛多年来最好的鸡鸡上所做的那一天。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 16. You must bet on cocks of your own group aside from mere loyalty considerations, for if you do not people generally will say, “What! Is he too proud for the likes of us? Does he have to go to Java or Den Pasar [the capital town] to bet, he is such an important man?” Thus there is a general pressure to bet not only to show that you are important locally, but that you are not so important that you look down on everyone else as unfit even to be rivals. Similarly, home team people must bet against outside cocks or the outsiders will accuse it–a serious charge–of just collecting entry fees and not really being interested in cockfighting, as well as again being arrogant and insulting.
blocks.zh: 16. 除了纯粹的忠诚度考虑之外，你还必须押注在自己组的雄鸽上，因为如果你不这样做，人们通常会说：“什么！他对我们这样的人来说太骄傲了吗？他必须去爪哇或登巴萨（首都）才能下注吗？他是如此重要的人物？”因此，人们普遍面临着打赌的压力，不仅是为了表明自己在当地很重要，而且还没有重要到看不起其他人，甚至认为自己不适合成为竞争对手。同样，主队的人必须与外面的公鸡打赌，否则外面的人会指责这种行为——这是一种严重的指控，因为他们只是收取入场费，而不是真正对斗鸡感兴趣，并且再次表现出傲慢和侮辱性。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 17. Finally, the Balinese peasants themselves are quite aware of all this and can and, at least to an ethnographer, do state most of it in approximately the same terms as I have. Fighting cocks, almost every Balinese I have ever discussed the subject with has said, is like playing with fire only not getting burned. You activate village and kingroup rivalries and hostilities, but in “play” form, coming dangerously and entrancingly close to the expression of open and direct interpersonal and intergroup aggression (something which, again, almost never happens in the normal course of ordinary life), but not quite, because, after all, it is “only a cockfight.”
blocks.zh: 17. 最后，巴厘岛农民自己非常清楚这一切，并且能够并且至少对于民族志学者来说确实能够用与我大致相同的术语来表述其中的大部分内容。几乎所有与我讨论过这个话题的巴厘岛人都说，斗鸡就像玩火，只是不会被烧伤。你激发了村庄和亲属群体的竞争和敌对行动，但以“游戏”的形式，危险而令人着迷地接近公开和直接的人际和群体间攻击的表达（这在日常生活的正常过程中几乎从未发生过），但又不完全是，因为毕竟，这“只是一场斗鸡”。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: More observations of this sort could be advanced, but perhaps the general point is, if not made, at least well-delineated, and the whole argument thus far can be usefully summarized in a formal paradigm:
blocks.zh: 可以提出更多此类观察，但也许一般观点即使没有提出，至少也得到了很好的描述，并且迄今为止的整个论点可以用一个正式的范式有效地总结：
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: the more a match is . . .
blocks.zh: 匹配越多。 。 。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 1. Between near status equals (and/or personal enemies)
blocks.zh: 1. 地位接近的平等者（和/或个人敌人）之间
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 2. Between high status individuals
blocks.zh: 2.地位高的人之间
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: the deeper the match.
blocks.zh: 比赛越深入。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: the deeper the match . . .
blocks.zh: 比赛越深入。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 1. The closer the identification of cock and man (or: more properly, the deeper the match the more the man will advance his best, most closely-identified-with cock).
blocks.zh: 1. 雄鸽和男子的认同越接近（或者：更准确地说，匹配越深入，男子就越能提升他最好的、与雄鸽最接近的认同）。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 2. The finer the cocks involved and the more exactly they will be matched.
blocks.zh: 2. 参与的雄鸽越优秀，它们的匹配就越精确。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 3. The greater the emotion that will be involved and the more the general absorption in the match.
blocks.zh: 3. 涉及的情绪越大，比赛的整体投入程度也越高。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 4. The higher the individual bets center and outside, the shorter the outside bet odds will tend to be, and the more betting there will be overall.
blocks.zh: 4. 中心和外围的个别投注越高，外围投注赔率往往越小，整体投注也越多。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: 5. The less an “economic” and the more a “status” view of gaming will be involved, and the “solider” the citizens who will be gaming.26
blocks.zh: 5. 博彩的“经济”观点越少，“地位”观点越多，参与博彩的公民就越“团结”。 26
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Inverse arguments hold for the shallower the fight, culminating, in a reversed-signs sense, in the coin-spinning and dice-throwing amusements. For deep fights there are no absolute upper limits, though there are of course practical ones, and there are a great many legend-like tales of great Duel-in-the-Sun combats between lords and princes in classical times (for cockfighting has always been as much an elite concern as a popular one), far deeper than anything
blocks.zh: 反向论证适用于较浅的战斗，从反向符号的意义上来说，最终以掷硬币和掷骰子的娱乐方式达到高潮。对于深入的战斗来说，没有绝对的上限，尽管当然也有实际的上限，而且古典时期有许多类似传奇般的领主和王子之间伟大的阳光下决斗的故事（因为斗鸡一直是精英阶层关注的事情，同时也是大众关注的事情），比任何事情都深刻得多
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Indeed, one of the great culture heroes of Bali is a prince, called after his passion for the sport, “The Cockfighter,” who happened to be away at a very deep cockfight with a neighboring prince when the whole of his family–father, brothers, wives, sisters–were assassinated by commoner usurpers. Thus spared, he returned to dispatch the upstarts, regain the throne, reconstitute the Balinese high tradition, and build its most powerful, glorious, and prosperous state. Along with everything else that the Balinese see in fighting cocks–themselves, their social order, abstract hatred, masculinity, demonic power–they also see the archetype of status virtue, the arrogant, resolute, honor-mad player with real fire, the ksatria prince.27
blocks.zh: 事实上，巴厘岛最伟大的文化英雄之一是一位王子，因其对这项运动的热情而被称为“斗鸡者”，当他的全家——父亲、兄弟、妻子、姐妹——被平民篡夺者暗杀时，他恰好在与邻近的一位王子进行一场非常激烈的斗鸡。如此幸免于难，他回来消灭暴发户，重新夺回王位，重建巴厘岛的崇高传统，并建立其最强大、光荣和繁荣的国家。除了巴厘岛人在斗鸡身上看到的一切——斗鸡本身、他们的社会秩序、抽象的仇恨、男子气概、恶魔的力量——他们还看到了地位美德的原型，傲慢、坚决、狂热的荣誉玩家，真正的火力，卡萨特里亚王子。 27
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Poetry makes nothing happen,” Auden says in his elegy of Yeats, “it survives in the valley of its saying . . . a way of happening, a mouth.” The cockfight too, in this colloquial sense, makes nothing happen. Men go on allegorically humiliating one another and being allegorically humiliated by one another, day after day, glorying quietly in the experience if they have triumphed, crushed only slightly more openly by it if they have not. But no one’s status really changes. You cannot ascend the status ladder by winning cockfights; you cannot, as an individual, really ascend it at all. Nor can you descend it that way.28 All you can do is enjoy and savor, or suffer and withstand, the concocted sensation of drastic and momentary movement along an aesthetic semblance of that ladder, a kind of behindthe-mirror status jump which has the look of mobility without its actuality.
blocks.zh: 诗歌不会发生任何事情，”奥登在他的叶芝挽歌中说道，“它在它的言说的山谷中幸存下来……。 。 。一种发生的方式，一张嘴。”从这个口语的意义上来说，斗鸡也没有发生任何事情。人们日复一日地继续寓言式地羞辱彼此，又被寓言式地羞辱，如果他们取得了胜利，他们就会在这种经历中默默地感到自豪，如果他们没有取得胜利，他们只会更加公开地被压垮。但没有人的地位真正改变。你不能通过赢得斗鸡来提升地位；作为一个个体，你根本无法真正提升它。你也不能用这种方式下降。28你所能做的就是享受和品味，或者忍受和承受，沿着梯子的美学外观剧烈而短暂的运动的混合感觉，一种镜子后面的地位跳跃，看起来有流动性，但实际上却没有。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As any art form–for that, finally, is what we are dealing with–the cockfight renders ordinary, everyday experience comprehensible by presenting it in terms of acts and objects which have had their practical consequences removed and been reduced (or, if you prefer, raised) to the level of sheer appearances, where their meaning can be more powerfully articulated and more exactly perceived. The cockfight is “really real” only to the cocks–it does not kill anyone, castrate anyone, reduce anyone to animal status, alter the hierarchical relations among people, nor refashion the hierarchy; it does not even redistribute income in any significant way. What it does is what, for other peoples with other temperaments and other conventions, Lear and Crime and Punishment do; it catches up these themes–death, masculinity, rage, pride, loss, beneficence, chance–and, ordering them into an encompassing structure, presents them in such a way as to throw into relief a particular view of their essential nature. It puts a construction on them, makes them, to those historically positioned to appreciate the construction, meaningful–visible, tangible, graspable–“real,” in an ideational sense. An image, fiction, a model, a metaphor, the cockfight is a means of expression; its function is neither to assuage social passions nor to heighten them (though, in its play-withfire way, it does a bit of both), but, in a medium of feathers, blood, crowds, and money, to display them.
blocks.zh: 与任何艺术形式一样——最后，这就是我们正在处理的——斗鸡通过以行为和物体的形式呈现普通的日常经验，使之变得可以理解，这些行为和物体已经消除了它们的实际后果，并被减少（或者，如果你愿意，提高）到纯粹的表象水平，在那里它们的意义可以被更强有力地表达和更准确地感知。斗鸡只对公鸡来说是“真正真实的”——它不会杀死任何人，阉割任何人，将任何人降低为动物地位，改变人与人之间的等级关系，也不会重塑等级；它不会杀死任何人，也不会阉割任何人。它甚至没有以任何重大方式重新分配收入。它所做的就是《李尔王》和《罪与罚》对于具有不同性情和不同习俗的其他民族所做的事情；它抓住了这些主题——死亡、男子气概、愤怒、骄傲、失落、仁慈、机会——并将它们整理成一个包容性的结构，以一种突显其本质本质的特殊观点的方式呈现它们。它对它们进行了建构，使它们对于那些历史上欣赏这种建构的人来说是有意义的——可见的、有形的、可理解的——在观念意义上是“真实的”。一个形象，一个虚构，一个模型，一个隐喻，斗鸡是一种表达方式；它的功能既不是平息社会激情，也不是煽动社会激情（尽管它以玩火的方式，两者兼而有之），而是以羽毛、鲜血、人群和金钱为媒介，展示它们。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The question of how it is that we perceive qualities in things–paintings, books, melodies, plays–that we do not feel we can assert literally to be there has come, in recent years, into the very center of aesthetic theory.29 Neither the sentiments of the artist, which remain his, nor those of the audience, which remain theirs, can account for the agitation of one painting or the serenity of another. We attribute grandeur, wit, despair, exuberance to strings of sounds; lightness, energy, violence, fluidity to blocks of stone. Novels are said to have strength, buildings eloquence, plays momentum, ballets repose. In this realm of eccentric predicates, to say that the cockfight, in its perfected cases at least, is “disquietful” does not seem at all unnatural, merely, as I have just denied it practical consequence, somewhat puzzling.
blocks.zh: 近年来，我们如何感知事物——绘画、书籍、旋律、戏剧——中我们感觉无法断言其存在的品质，这个问题已经成为美学理论的核心。29艺术家的情感（仍然是他的）和观众的情感（仍然是他们的）都无法解释一幅画的激动或另一幅画的平静。我们把宏伟、机智、绝望、活力归因于声音的串串；石块的轻盈、能量、暴力、流动性。据说小说有力量，建筑有口才，戏剧有气势，芭蕾有休止符。在这个古怪谓词的领域中，说斗鸡，至少在其完美的情况下，是“令人不安的”，似乎一点也不不自然，只是，正如我刚刚否认的那样，它的实际后果有点令人费解。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The disquietfulness arises, “somehow,” out of a conjunction of three attributes of the fight: its immediate dramatic shape; its metaphoric content; and its social context. A cultural
blocks.zh: “不知何故”，这种不安是由战斗的三个属性结合在一起产生的：它直接的戏剧性的形式；它的隐喻内容；及其社会背景。一个文化
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As a dramatic shape, the fight displays a characteristic that does not seem so remarkable until one realizes that it does not have to be there: a radically atomistical structure.30 Each match is a world unto itself, a particulate burst of form. There is the match making, there is the betting, there is the fight, there is the result–utter triumph and utter defeat– and there is the hurried, embarrassed passing of money. The loser is not consoled. People drift away from him, look through him, leave him to assimilate his momentary descent into nonbeing, reset his face, and return, scarless and intact, to the fray. Nor are winners congratulated, or events rehashed; once a match is ended the crowd’s attention turns totally to the next, with no looking back. A shadow of the experience no doubt remains with the principals, perhaps even with some of the witnesses, of a deep fight, as it remains with us when we leave the theater after seeing a powerful play well-performed; but it quite soon fades to become at most a schematic memory–a diffuse glow or an abstract shudder–and usually not even that. Any expressive form lives only in its own present–the one it itself creates. But, here, that present is severed into a string of flashes, some more bright than others, but all of them disconnected, aesthetic quanta. Whatever the cockfight says, it says in spurts.
blocks.zh: 作为一种戏剧性的形式，这场战斗展现了一种看似并不那么引人注目的特征，直到人们意识到它不一定存在：一种根本上的原子结构。30 每场比赛都是一个独立的世界，是形式的微粒爆发。有牵线搭桥，有投注，有战斗，有结果——彻底的胜利和彻底的失败——还有匆忙、尴尬的金钱传递。失败者得不到安慰。人们渐渐远离他，看透他，让他将短暂的堕落同化为虚无，重新调整他的面容，然后毫发无伤地回到战斗中。获奖者也不会得到祝贺，事件也不会被重新讨论；一旦一场比赛结束，观众的注意力就会完全转向下一场比赛，不会回头。毫无疑问，一场深刻的战斗的经历的阴影仍然存在于主要人物身上，甚至可能存在于一些目击者身上，就像当我们在看完一场精彩的戏剧表演后离开剧院时，它仍然存在于我们身上一样。但它很快就会消失，至多成为一种示意性记忆——一种弥漫的光芒或一种抽象的颤抖——而且通常甚至不是这样。任何表达形式都只存在于它自己的当下——它自己创造的当下。但是，在这里，那个当下被分割成一串闪光，有些比其他更亮，但所有这些都是互不相连的，美学量子。无论斗鸡说什么，它都会突然说出来。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: But, as I have argued lengthily elsewhere, the Balinese live in spurts.31 Their life, as they arrange it and perceive it, is less a flow, a directional movement out of the past, through the present, toward the future than an on-off pulsation of meaning and vacuity, an arrhythmic alternation of short periods when “something” (that is, something significant) is happening and equally short ones where “nothing” (that is, nothing much) is–between what they themselves call “full” and “empty” times, or, in another idiom, “junctures” and “holes.” In focusing activity down to a burning-glass dot, the cockfight is merely being Balinese in the same way in which everything from the monadic encounters of everyday life, through the clanging pointillism of gamelan music, to the visiting-day-of-the-gods temple celebrations are. It is not an imitation of the punctuateness of Balinese social life, nor a depiction of it, nor even an expression of it; it is an example of it, carefully prepared.32
blocks.zh: 但是，正如我在其他地方长时间论证的那样，巴厘岛人的生活充满了爆发力。 31他们的生活，在他们安排和感知的过程中，与其说是一种流动，一种从过去、穿过现在、走向未来的定向运动，不如说是一种意义和空虚的开关脉动，一种“有事”（即重大事件）发生的短暂时期和“无事”（即没有什么大事）发生的同样短暂的短暂时期的无节律交替。他们自己称之为“满”和“空”时间，或者用另一个习语来说，“接合点”和“洞”。将活动集中到一个燃烧的玻璃点上，斗鸡只是巴厘岛人的方式，就像日常生活中的单子相遇，通过甘美兰音乐的叮叮当当的点彩派，到众神来访的寺庙庆祝活动一样。它不是对巴厘岛社会生活准时性的模仿，也不是对它的描述，甚至不是它的表达；它是一种表达。这是精心准备的一个例子。32
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: If one dimension of the cockfight’s structure, its lack of temporal directionality, makes it seem a typical segment of the general social life, however, the other, its flat-out, head-to-head (or spur-tospur) aggressiveness, makes it seem a contradiction, a reversal, even a subversion of it. In the normal course of things, the Balinese are shy to the point of obsessiveness of open conflict. Oblique, cautious, subdued, controlled, masters of indirection and dissimulation–what they call alus, “polished,” “smooth”– they rarely face what they can turn away from, rarely resist what they can evade. But here they portray themselves as wild and murderous, manic explosions of instinctual cruelty. A powerful rendering of life as the Balinese most deeply do not want it (to adapt a phrase Frye has used of Gloucester’s blinding) is set in the context of a sample of it as they do in fact have it.33 And, because the context suggests that the rendering, if less than a straightforward description is nonetheless more than an idle fancy, it is here that the disquietfulness–the disquietfulness of the fight, not (or, anyway, not necessarily) its patrons, who seem in fact rather thoroughly to enjoy it– emerges. The slaughter in the cock ring is not a depiction of how things literally are among men, but, what is almost worse, of how, from a particular angle, they imaginatively are.34
blocks.zh: 如果说斗鸡结构的一个方面，即它缺乏时间方向性，使它看起来是一般社会生活的一个典型部分，那么，另一方面，它的直截了当的、头对头（或马刺-马刺）的攻击性，则使它看起来是一种矛盾、一种逆转，甚至是一种颠覆。在正常情况下，巴厘岛人羞于公开冲突。狡猾、谨慎、克制、克制，是间接和掩饰的大师——他们称之为alus、“优雅”、“圆滑”——他们很少面对他们可以逃避的事情，很少抵制他们可以逃避的事情。但在这里，他们把自己描绘成狂野、凶残、本能残忍的狂躁爆发。对巴厘岛人最不想要的生活的有力渲染（改编为弗莱在格洛斯特致盲时使用的短语）是在他们实际上拥有的样本的背景下设定的。33而且，因为上下文表明，这种渲染，如果不是一个简单的描述，但仍然只是一种无聊的幻想，那么这里的不安——战斗的不安，而不是（或者，无论如何，不一定）它的赞助人，他们实际上似乎是这样的。相当彻底地享受它——出现了。公鸡圈中的屠杀并不是对人类之间事物真实情况的描述，但更糟糕的是，从特定角度来看，它们在想象中是如何存在的。 34

blocks.zh: 当然，角度是分层的。正如我们已经看到的，斗鸡最有力地谈论的是地位关系，它所表达的是它们是生死攸关的问题。这种威望是亲

blocks.en: Any expressive form works (when it works) by disarranging semantic contexts in such a way that properties conventionally ascribed to certain things are unconventionally ascribed to others, which are then seen actually to possess them. To call the wind a cripple, as Stevens does, to fix tone and manipulate timbre, as Schoenberg does, or, closer to our case, to picture an art critic as a dissolute bear, as Hogarth does, is to cross conceptual wires; the established conjunctions between objects and their qualities are altered and phenomena– fall weather, melodic shape, or cultural journalism–are clothed in signifiers which normally point to other referents.35 Similarly, to connect–and connect, and connect–the collision of roosters with the divisiveness of status is to invite a transfer of perceptions from the former to the latter, a transfer which is at once a description and a judgment. (Logically, the transfer could, of course, as well go the other way; but, like most of the rest of us, the Balinese are a great deal more interested in understanding men than they are in understanding cocks.)
blocks.zh: 任何表达形式（当它起作用时）都是通过打乱语义上下文来起作用的，这种方式使得传统上归因于某些事物的属性被非常规地归因于其他事物，然后被视为实际上拥有它们。像史蒂文斯那样称风为跛子，像勋伯格那样固定音调和操纵音色，或者更接近我们的情况，像霍加斯那样将艺术评论家描绘成放荡的熊，都是跨越概念的界限；物体及其品质之间既定的联系发生了改变，现象——秋天的天气、旋律的形状或文化新闻——被披上了通常指向其他指称的能指的外衣。 35同样，将公鸡与地位的分裂性的碰撞连接起来——连接起来，再连接起来，就是邀请从前者到后者的感知转移，这种转移既是一种描述，也是一种判断。 （从逻辑上讲，这种转移当然也可以反其道而行之；但是，像我们大多数人一样，巴厘岛人对了解男人比了解鸡巴更感兴趣。）
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: What sets the cockfight apart from the ordinary course of life, lifts it from the realm of everyday practical affairs, and surrounds it with an aura of enlarged importance is not, as functionalist sociology would have it, that it reinforces status discriminations (such reinforcement is hardly necessary in a society where every act proclaims them), but that it provides a metasocial commentary upon the whole matter of assorting human beings into fixed hierarchical ranks and then organizing the major part of collective existence around that assortment. Its function, if you want to call it that, is interpretive: it is a Balinese reading of Balinese experience; a story they tell themselves about themselves.
blocks.zh: 使斗鸡区别于日常生活、将其从日常实际事务领域中抽离出来、并赋予它更大重要性的光环的，并不是像功能主义社会学所认为的那样，它强化了地位歧视（在一个每项行为都宣扬地位歧视的社会中，这种强化几乎是不必要的），而是它为将人类划分为固定的等级等级，然后围绕这种分类组织集体存在的主要部分的整个问题提供了一种元社会评论。如果你想这样称呼它的话，它的功能是解释性的：它是对巴厘岛经验的巴厘岛式解读；他们讲述自己的故事。
blocks.translation_method: retained-previous-translation

blocks.en: To put the matter this way is to engage in a bit of metaphorical refocusing of one’s own, for it shifts the analysis of cultural forms from an endeavor in general parallel to dissecting an organism, diagnosing a symptom, deciphering a code, or ordering a system–the dominant analogies in contemporary anthropology–to one in general parallel with penetrating a literary text. If one takes the cockfight, or any other collectively sustained symbolic structure, as a means of “saying something of something” (to invoke a famous Aristotelian tag), then one is faced with a problem not in social mechanics but social semantics.36 For the anthropologist, whose concern is with formulating sociological principles, not with promoting or appreciating cockfights, the question is, what does one learn about such principles from examining culture as an assemblage of texts?
blocks.zh: 这样说，就是对自己的隐喻进行了重新定位，因为它将对文化形式的分析从一般与解剖有机体、诊断症状、破译密码或整理系统（当代人类学中占主导地位的类比）平行的努力转变为与洞察文学文本一般平行的分析。如果一个人将斗鸡或任何其他集体维持的象征结构视为“说某事”的一种手段（援引一个著名的亚里士多德标签），那么我们面临的问题就不是社会机制的问题，而是社会语义学的问题。 36对于人类学家来说，他们关心的是制定社会学原理，而不是促进或欣赏斗鸡，问题是，通过将文化作为文本的集合来考察，人们可以从这些原则中学到什么？
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Such an extension of the notion of a text beyond written material, and even beyond verbal, is, though metaphorical, not, of course, all that novel. The interpretatio naturae tradition of the Middle Ages, which, culminating in Spinoza, attempted to read nature as Scripture, the Nietszchean effort to treat value systems as glosses on the will to power (or the Marxian one to treat them as glosses on property relations), and the Freudian replacement of the enigmatic text of the manifest dream with the plain one of the latent, all offer precedents, if not equally recommendable ones.37 But the idea remains theoretically undeveloped; and the more profound corollary, so far as anthropology is concerned, that cultural forms can be treated as texts, as imaginative works built out of social materials, has yet to be systematically exploited.38
blocks.zh: 文本概念的这种延伸超出了书面材料，甚至超出了口头材料，尽管是隐喻性的，但当然并不是那么新颖。中世纪的自然解释传统，在斯宾诺莎试图将自然解读为《圣经》，这一传统在斯宾诺莎那里达到顶峰，尼采试图将价值体系视为对权力意志的注解（或者马克思主义将其视为对财产关系的注解），以及弗洛伊德用朴素的潜在文本取代显梦的神秘文本，所有这些都提供了先例，即使不是同样值得推荐的先例。 37但这一想法在理论上仍然没有发展；就人类学而言，更深刻的推论，即文化形式可以被视为文本，被视为由社会材料构建的富有想象力的作品，尚未得到系统的利用。 38
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In the case at hand, to treat the cockfight as a text is to bring out a feature of it (in my opinion, the central feature of it) that treating it as a rite or a pastime, the two most obvious alternatives, would tend to obscure: its use of emotion for cognitive ends. What the cockfight says it says in a vocabulary of sentiment–the thrill of risk, the despair of loss, the pleasure of triumph. Yet what it says is not merely that risk is exciting, loss depressing, or triumph gratifying, banal tautologies of affect, but that it is of these emotions, thus exampled, that society is built and individuals put together. Attending cockfights and participating in them is, for the Balinese, a kind of sentimental education. What he learns there is what his culture’s ethos and his private sensibility (or, anyway, certain aspects of them) look like when spelled out externally in a collective text; that the two are near enough alike to be articulated in the symbolics of a single such text; and–the disquieting part–that the text in which this revelation is accomplished consists of a
blocks.zh: 就目前的情况而言，将斗鸡视为一种文本，是为了凸显它的一个特征（在我看来，这是它的核心特征），即把它视为一种仪式或一种消遣，这两个最明显的选择，往往会变得模糊：它利用情感来达到认知目的。斗鸡所表达的情感是一种情感词汇——冒险的兴奋、失败的绝望、胜利的喜悦。然而，它所说的不仅仅是风险令人兴奋，损失令人沮丧，或胜利令人欣慰，情感的平庸同义反复，而且正是这些情感，如此例证，社会得以建立，个人聚集在一起。观看斗鸡并参与其中，对于巴厘岛人来说，是一种情感教育。他在那里学到的是他的文化的精神和他的私人情感（或者，无论如何，它们的某些方面）在集体文本中外部阐明时的样子；两者非常相似，可以用一个这样的文本的象征意义来表达；并且——令人不安的部分——完成这一启示的文本由
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Every people, the proverb has it, loves its own form of violence. The cockfight is the Balinese reflection on theirs: on its look, its uses, its force, its fascination. Drawing on almost every level of Balinese experience, it brings together themes–animal savagery, male narcissism, opponent gambling, status rivalry, mass excitement, blood sacrifice– whose main connection is their involvement with rage and the fear of rage, and, binding them into a set of rules which at once contains them and allows them play, builds a symbolic structure in which, over and over again, the reality of their inner affiliation can be intelligibly felt. If, to quote Northrop Frye again, we go to see Macbeth to learn what a man feels like after he has gained a kingdom and lost his soul, Balinese go to cockfights to find out what a man, usually composed, aloof, almost obsessively self-absorbed, a kind of moral autocosm, feels like when, attacked, tormented, challenged, insulted, and driven in result to the extremes of fury, he has totally triumphed or been brought totally low. The whole passage, as it takes us back to Aristotle (though to the Poetics rather than the Hermeneutics), is worth quotation:
blocks.zh: 俗话说，每个民族都喜欢自己的暴力形式。斗鸡是巴厘岛人对斗鸡的反思：它的外观、它的用途、它的力量和它的魅力。它借鉴了巴厘岛人几乎各个层面的经验，汇集了主题——动物的野蛮、男性自恋、对手赌博、地位竞争、大众兴奋、血腥牺牲——其主要联系是他们对愤怒的参与和对愤怒的恐惧，并将它们绑定到一套既包含它们又允许它们玩耍的规则中，构建了一个象征性结构，在这个象征性结构中，人们可以一遍又一遍地清晰地感受到他们内心归属的现实。如果，再次引用诺斯罗普·弗莱的话，如果我们去看麦克白，了解一个人在获得王国并失去灵魂后的感受，那么巴厘岛人去斗鸡，了解一个通常沉着、冷漠、几乎痴迷于自我中心、一种道德自体的人，在受到攻击、折磨、挑战、侮辱，并最终被逼到极端愤怒时，他的感觉是怎样的，他已经完全胜利或被带入了。完全低。整段话将我们带回到亚里士多德（尽管是诗学而不是诠释学），值得引用：

blocks.en: But the poet [as opposed to the historian], Aristotle says, never makes any real statements at all, certainly no particular or specific ones. The poet’s job is not to tell you what happened, but what happens: not what did take place, but the kind of thing that always does take place. He gives you the typical, recurring, or what Aristotle calls universal event. You wouldn’t go to Macbeth to learn about the history of Scotland–you go to it to learn what a man feels like after he’s gained a kingdom and lost his soul. When you meet
blocks.zh: 但亚里士多德说，诗人（相对于历史学家）从来没有做出任何真实的陈述，当然也没有具体的或具体的陈述。诗人的工作不是告诉你发生了什么，而是告诉你发生了什么：不是已经发生了什么，而是总是发生的事情。他为你提供了典型的、反复出现的、或者亚里士多德所说的普遍事件。你不会去《麦克白》了解苏格兰的历史——你去它是为了了解一个人在获得王国并失去灵魂后的感受。当你遇见
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: such a character as Micawber in Dickens, you don’t feel that there must have been a man Dickens knew who was exactly like this: you feel that there’s a bit of Micawber in almost everybody you know, including yourself. Our impressions of human life are picked up one by one, and remain for most of us loose and disorganized. But we constantly find things in literature that suddenly co-ordinate and bring into focus a great many such impressions, and this is part of what Aristotle means by the typical or universal human event.39
blocks.zh: 狄更斯笔下的米考伯这样的人物，你不会觉得狄更斯认识的人一定是这样的：你觉得你认识的几乎每个人，包括你自己，都有一点米考伯的影子。我们对人类生活的印象是一一积累的，对我们大多数人来说仍然是松散和杂乱的。但我们不断地在文学中发现一些东西，这些东西突然协调并集中了许多这样的印象，这就是亚里士多德所说的典型或普遍的人类事件的一部分。 39
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It is this kind of bringing of assorted experiences of everyday life to focus that the cockfight, set aside from that life as “only a game” and reconnected to it as “more than a game,” accomplishes, and so creates what, better than typical or universal, could be called a paradigmatic human event– that is, one that tells us less what happens than the kind of thing that would happen if, as is not the case, life were art and could be as freely shaped by styles of feeling as Macbeth and David Copperfield are.
blocks.zh: 正是这种将日常生活中的各种经历集中在一起的方式，使斗鸡脱离了生活，将其视为“只是一场游戏”，并将其重新连接为“不仅仅是一场游戏”，从而创造了比典型或普遍的更好的人类事件范例——也就是说，它告诉我们的不是发生了什么，而是如果生活是艺术，并且可以像麦克白和大卫那样被感觉风格自由塑造，而不是告诉我们会发生什么事情。科波菲尔是。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Enacted and reenacted, so far without end, the cockfight enables the Balinese, as, read and reread, Macbeth enables us, to see a dimension of his own subjectivity. As he watches fight after fight with the active watching of an owner and a bettor (for cockfighting has no more interest as a pure spectator sport than croquet or dog racing do), he grows familiar with it and what it has to say to him, much as the attentive listener to string quartets or the absorbed viewer of still lifes grows slowly more familiar with them in a way which opens his subjectivity to himself.40
blocks.zh: 斗鸡一再上演，至今永无休止，它让巴厘岛人看到了他自己主观性的一个维度，就像读了又重读的《麦克白》一样，它让我们看到了他自己的主观性。当他在主人和投注者的积极观看下观看一场又一场的战斗时（因为斗鸡作为一种纯粹的观赏性运动，并不比槌球或赛狗更有兴趣），他逐渐熟悉了它以及它对他说的话，就像弦乐四重奏的细心聆听者或静物画的全神贯注的观众以一种向自己开放主观性的方式慢慢地更加熟悉它们一样。 40
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Yet, because–in another of those paradoxes, along with painted feelings and unconsequenced acts, which haunt aesthetics–that subjectivity does not properly exist until it is thus organized, art forms generate and regenerate the very subjectivity they pretend only to display. Quartets, still lifes, and cockfights are not merely reflections of a preexisting sensibility analogically represented; they are positive agents in the creation and maintenance of such a sensibility. If we see ourselves as a pack of Micawbers it is from reading too much Dickens (if we see ourselves as unillusioned realists, it is from reading too little); and similarly for Balinese, cocks, and cockfights. It is in such a way, coloring experience with the light they cast it in, rather than through whatever material effects they may have, that the arts play their role, as arts, in social life.41
blocks.zh: 然而，因为——在另一个悖论中，连同描绘的情感和无关紧要的行为，困扰着美学——主观性只有在如此组织起来之后才能正确存在，艺术形式产生并再生了它们假装只是展示的主观性。四重奏、静物画和斗鸡不仅是类比代表的先前存在的情感的反映；它们是创造和维持这种情感的积极推动者。如果我们把自己视为一群米考伯，那是因为读了太多狄更斯的作品（如果我们把自己视为不抱幻想的现实主义者，那是因为读得太少了）；巴厘岛人、公鸡和斗鸡也是如此。正是通过这样一种方式，艺术通过它们所投射的光线来着色经验，而不是通过它们可能具有的任何物质效果，在社会生活中发挥其作为艺术的作用。 41
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In the cockfight, then, the Balinese forms and discovers his temperament and his society’s temper at the same time. Or, more exactly, he forms and discovers a particular face of them. Not only are there a great many other cultural texts providing commentaries on status hierarchy and self-regard in Bali, but there are a great many other critical sectors of Balinese life besides the stratificatory and the agonistic that receive such commentary. The ceremony consecrating a Brahmana priest, a matter of breath control, postural immobility, and vacant concentration upon the depths of being, displays a radically different, but to the Balinese equally real, property of social hierarchy–its reach toward the numinous transcendent. Set not in the matrix of the kinetic emotionality of animals, but in that of the static passionlessness of divine mentality, it expresses tranquility not disquiet. The mass festivals at the village temples, which mobilize the whole local population in elaborate hostings of visiting gods–songs, dances, compliments, gifts–assert the spiritual unity of village mates against their status inequality and project a mood of amity and trust.42 The cockfight is not the master key to Balinese life, any more than bullfighting is to Spanish. What it says about that life is not unqualified nor even unchallenged by what other equally eloquent cultural statements say about it. But there is nothing more surprising in this than in the fact that Racine and Molière were contemporaries, or that the same people who arrange chrysanthemums cast swords.43
blocks.zh: 那么，在斗鸡中，巴厘岛人同时形成并发现了自己的气质和社会脾气。或者，更准确地说，他形成并发现了它们的特定面孔。不仅有许多其他文化文本提供了对巴厘岛地位等级和自尊的评论，而且除了分层和竞争之外，巴厘岛人生活的许多其他关键领域也接受了此类评论。婆罗门祭司的祝圣仪式，涉及呼吸控制、姿势不动以及对存在深处的空虚专注，展示了一种截然不同的、但对巴厘岛人来说同样真实的社会等级属性——它对超然的神圣影响。它不是以动物的动态情感为母体，而是以神圣心态的静态无激情为母体，它表达的是宁静而不是不安。村庄寺庙里的群众节日动员全体当地居民精心招待来访的神灵——歌曲、舞蹈、赞美、礼物——维护了村里成员的精神团结，反对他们的地位不平等，并表现出一种友好和信任的气氛。 42斗鸡不是巴厘岛人生活的万能钥匙，就像斗牛不是西班牙人的万能钥匙一样。它对生命的描述并非没有资格，甚至不受其他同样雄辩的文化陈述的质疑。但最令人惊讶的莫过于拉辛和莫里哀是同时代人，或者是同一群安排菊花的人铸造了剑。 43
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The culture of a people is an ensemble of texts, themselves ensembles, which the anthropologist strains to read over the shoulders of those to whom they properly belong. There are enormous difficulties in such an enterprise, methodological pitfalls to make a Freudian quake, and some moral perplexities as well. Nor is it the only way that symbolic forms can be sociologically handled. Functionalism lives, and so does psychologism. But to regard such forms as “saying something of something,” and saying it to somebody, is at least to open up the possibility of an analysis which attends to their substance rather than to reductive formulas professing to account for them.
blocks.zh: 一个民族的文化是文本的集合，其本身就是集合，人类学家竭尽全力地在他们所属的人的肩膀上阅读它们。这样的事业存在着巨大的困难，方法论上的陷阱足以引发弗洛伊德式的震动，而且还存在一些道德上的困惑。这也不是社会学处理符号形式的唯一方法。功能主义依然存在，心理主义也同样存在。但是，将这些形式视为“对某事说某事”，并向某人说，至少开启了一种分析的可能性，这种分析关注它们的实质，而不是声称可以解释它们的简化公式。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: As in more familiar exercises in close reading, one can start anywhere in a culture’s repertoire of forms and end up anywhere else. One can stay, as I have here, within a single, more or less bounded form and circle steadily within it. One can move between forms in search of broader unities or informing contrasts. One can even compare forms from different cultures to define their character in reciprocal relief. But whatever the level at which one operates, and however intricately, the guiding principle is the same: societies, like lives, contain their own interpretations. One has only to learn how to gain access to them.
blocks.zh: 正如在更熟悉的细读练习中一样，人们可以从一种文化的形式库中的任何地方开始，然后以其他地方结束。就像我在这里一样，一个人可以停留在一个单一的、或多或少有限制的形式内，并在其中稳定地循环。人们可以在各种形式之间移动，以寻找更广泛的统一性或鲜明的对比。人们甚至可以比较不同文化的形式，以相互理解的方式来定义它们的特征。但无论一个人的运作水平如何，无论多么复杂，指导原则都是相同的：社会就像生活一样，有自己的解释。人们只需学习如何获得它们。

blocks.en: 4 Ibid., 25–26. The cockfight is unusual within Balinese culture in being a single sex public activity from which the other sex is totally and expressly excluded. Sexual differentiation is culturally extremely played down in Bali and most activities, formal and informal, involve the participation of men and women on equal ground, commonly as linked couples. From religion, to politics, to economics, to kinship, to dress, Bali is a rather “unisex” society, a fact both its customs and its symbolism clearly express. Even in contexts where women do not in fact play much of a role–music, painting, certain agricultural activities–their absence, which is only relative in any case, is more a mere matter of fact than socially enforced. To this general pattern, the cockfight, entirely of, by, and for men (women–at least Balinese women–do not even watch), is the most striking exception.
blocks.zh: 4 同上，25-26。斗鸡在巴厘岛文化中很不寻常，因为它是一种单一性别的公共活动，异性完全被明确排除在外。在巴厘岛，性别差异在文化上被极度淡化，大多数正式和非正式的活动都涉及男性和女性在平等的基础上参与，通常是作为相连的夫妻。从宗教、政治、经济、亲属关系到服饰，巴厘岛是一个相当“男女皆宜”的社会，其习俗和象征意义都清楚地表达了这一事实。即使在妇女实际上并没有发挥多大作用的环境中——音乐、绘画、某些农业活动——她们的缺席在任何情况下都只是相对的，更多的是一个事实问题，而不是社会强制的。相对于这种普遍模式，斗鸡是最引人注目的例外，它完全由男性主导、由男性主导、为男性服务（女性——至少是巴厘岛女性——甚至不观看）。

blocks.en: 9 Except for unimportant, small-bet fights (on the question of fight “importance,” see below) spur affixing is usually done by someone other than the owner. Whether the owner handles his own cock or not more or less depends on how skilled he is at it, a consideration whose importance is again relative to the importance of the fight. When spur affixers and cock handlers are someone other than the owner, they are almost always a quite close relative–a brother or cousin–or a very intimate friend of his. They are thus almost extensions of his personality, as the fact that all three will refer to the cock as “mine,” say “I” fought So-and-So, and so on, demonstrates. Also, owner-handler-affixer triads tend to be fairly fixed, though individuals may participate in several and often exchange roles within a given one.
blocks.zh: 9 除了不重要的小额打斗（关于打斗“重要性”的问题，见下文）外，固定马刺通常是由除主人以外的其他人进行的。主人是否处理自己的鸡鸡或多或少取决于他的熟练程度，这一考虑的重要性又与战斗的重要性相关。当马刺固定者和公鸡处理者不是主人时，他们几乎总是他的近亲——兄弟或表兄弟——或者是他的非常亲密的朋友。因此，它们几乎是他个性的延伸，事实证明，这三个人都会将公鸡称为“我的”，说“我”与某某打斗，等等。此外，所有者-处理者-固定者三合会往往是相当固定的，尽管个人可能会参与多个角色，并且经常在一个给定的角色中交换角色。

blocks.en: 11 This word, which literally means an indelible stain or mark, as in a birthmark or a vein in a stone, is used as well for a deposit in a court case, for a pawn, for security offered in a loan, for a stand-in for someone else in a legal or ceremonial context, for an earnest advanced in a business deal, for a sign placed in a field to indicate its ownership is in dispute, and for the status of an unfaithful wife from whose lover her husband must gain satisfaction or surrender her to him. See Korn, Het Adatrecht van Bali; Theodoor Pigeaud, Javaans-Nederlands Handwoordenboek (Groningen: Wolters, 1938); H. H. Juynboll, Oudjavaansche-Nederlandsche Woordenlijst (Leiden: Brill, 1923).
blocks.zh: 11 这个词的字面意思是不可磨灭的污点或印记，如胎记或石头上的静脉，也可用于法庭案件中的押金、典当、贷款中提供的担保、法律或礼仪场合中的其他人的替身、商业交易中的真诚预付款、放置在田野上以表明其所有权存在争议的标志，以及不忠的妻子的地位，她的丈夫必须从其情人那里获得满足或满意。将她交给他。参见 Korn，Het Adatrecht van Bali； Theodoor Pigeaud，Javaans-Nederlands Handwoordenboek（格罗宁根：Wolters，1938）； H. H. Juynboll，《Oudjavaansche-Nederlandsche Woordenlijst》（莱顿：布里尔，1923 年）。

blocks.en: 12 The center bet must be advanced in cash by both parties prior to the actual fight. The umpire holds the stakes until the decision is rendered and then awards them to the winner, avoiding, among other things, the intense embarrassment both winner and loser would feel if the latter had to pay off personally following his defeat. About 10 percent of the winner’s receipts are subtracted for the umpire’s share and that of the fight sponsors.
blocks.zh: 12 中间投注必须由双方在实际比赛前以现金预付。裁判员持有赌注，直到做出决定，然后将赌注奖励给获胜者，这样可以避免获胜者和失败者在失败后必须亲自偿还时感到的强烈尴尬。获胜者收入的大约 10% 会扣除裁判员和比赛赞助商的份额。

blocks.en: 13 Actually, the typing of cocks, which is extremely elaborate (I have collected more than twenty classes, certainly not a complete list), is not based on color alone, but on a series of independent, interacting, dimensions, which include, beside color, size, bone thickness, plumage, and temperament. (But not pedigree. The Balinese do not breed cocks to any significant extent, nor, so far as I have been able to discover, have they ever done so. The asil, or jungle cock, which is the basic fighting strain everywhere the sport is found, is native to southern Asia, and one can buy a good example in the chicken section of almost any Balinese market for anywhere from 4 or 5 ringgits up to 50 or more.) The color element is merely the one normally used as the type name, except when the two cocks of different types–as on principle they must be–have the same color, in which case a secondary indication from one of the other dimensions (“large speckled” v. “small speckled,” etc.) is added. The types are coordinated with various cosmological ideas which help shape the making of matches, so that, for example, you fight a small, headstrong, speckled brown-on-white cock with flat-lying feathers and thin legs from the east side of the ring on a certain day of the complex Balinese calendar, and a large, cautious, all-black cock with tufted feathers and stubby legs from the north side on another day, and so on. All this is again recorded in palm-leaf manuscripts and endlessly discussed by the Balinese (who do not all have identical systems), and full-scale componential-cum-symbolic analysis of cock classifications would be extremely valuable both as an adjunct to the description of the cockfight and in itself. But my data on the subject, though extensive and varied, do not seem to be complete and systematic enough to attempt such an analysis here. For Balinese cosmological ideas more generally see Belo, ed., Traditional Balinese Culture, and J. L. Swellengrebel, ed., Bali: Studies in Life, Thought, and Ritual (The Hague: W. van Hoeve, 1960); for calendrical ones, Clifford Geertz, Person, Time, and Conduct in Bali: An Essay in Cultural Analysis (New Haven, Conn.: Southeast Asia Studies, Yale University, 1966), 45–53.
blocks.zh: 13 事实上，公鸡的分类是极其复杂的（我收集了二十多个类别，当然不是完整的列表），它不仅仅基于颜色，而是基于一系列独立的、相互作用的维度，除了颜色之外，还包括大小、骨骼厚度、羽毛和气质。 （但不是血统。巴厘岛人没有在很大程度上饲养公鸡，据我所知，他们也没有这样做过。丛林公鸡是这项运动随处可见的基本格斗品系，原产于南亚，人们可以在几乎任何巴厘岛市场的鸡肉区买到一只很好的例子，价格从 4 或 5 林吉特到 50 林吉特或更多。）颜色元素只是通常用作类型的元素。名称，除非两只不同类型的公鸡（原则上它们必须如此）具有相同的颜色，在这种情况下，添加来自其他维度之一的辅助指示（“大斑点”与“小斑点”等）。这些类型与有助于塑造比赛制作的各种宇宙学思想相协调，因此，例如，您可以在复杂的巴厘岛日历的某一天与来自环东侧的一只小而任性、有斑点的棕白公鸡进行战斗，这只公鸡具有平躺的羽毛和细腿，而在另一天与来自北侧的一只大而谨慎的全黑公鸡进行战斗，它有簇状羽毛和粗短的腿，等等。所有这些都再次记录在棕榈叶手稿中，并被巴厘岛人（他们并不都有相同的系统）无休止地讨论，而对公鸡分类的全面成分和符号分析将非常有价值，无论是作为斗鸡描述的辅助还是斗鸡本身。但我关于这个主题的数据虽然广泛且多样，但似乎并不足够完整和系统，可以在这里尝试这样的分析。对于巴厘岛的宇宙论思想，请参阅 Belo 编辑的《传统巴厘岛文化》和 J. L. Swellengrebel 编辑的《巴厘岛：生活、思想和仪式研究》（海牙：W. van Hoeve，1960 年）；对于日历，Clifford Geertz，巴厘岛的人物、时间和行为：文化分析论文（康涅狄格州纽黑文：东南亚研究，耶鲁大学，1966 年），45-53。

blocks.en: 14 For purposes of ethnographic completeness, it should be noted that it is possible for the man backing the favorite–the odds-giver –to make a bet in which he wins if his cock wins or there is a tie, a slight shortening of the odds (I do not have enough cases to be exact, but ties seem to occur about once every fifteen or twenty matches). He indicates his wish to do this by shouting sapih (“tie”) rather than the cock-type, but such bets are in fact infrequent.
blocks.zh: 14 出于人种学完整性的目的，应该指出的是，支持热门球队的人（赔率提供者）可以下注，如果他的雄鸽获胜或出现平局，则他获胜，赔率略有缩短（我没有足够的案例来准确说明，但平局似乎大约每十五或二十场比赛就会发生一次）。他通过喊“sapih”（“领带”）而不是“公鸡”来表达他的愿望，但实际上这样的赌注并不常见。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 15 The precise dynamics of the movement of the betting is one of the most intriguing, most complicated, and, given the hectic conditions under which it occurs, most difficult to study, aspects of the fight. Motion picture recording plus multiple observers would probably be necessary to deal with it effectively. Even impressionistically–the only approach open to a lone ethnographer caught in the middle of all this– it is clear that certain men lead both in determining the favorite (that is, making the opening cock-type calls which always initiate the process) and in directing the movement of the odds, these “opinion leaders” being the more accomplished cockfighters-cum-solid-citizens to be discussed below. If these men begin to change their calls, others follow; if they begin to make bets, so do others and–though there is always a large number of frustrated bettors crying for shorter or longer odds to the end– the movement more or less ceases. But a detailed understanding of the whole process awaits what, alas, it is not very likely ever to get: a decision theorist armed with precise observations of individual behavior.
blocks.zh: 15 投注运动的精确动态是战斗中最有趣、最复杂的方面之一，而且考虑到比赛发生的繁忙条件，也是最难研究的方面。为了有效地处理这个问题，可能需要动态图像录制加上多个观察者。即使是印象派——这是对陷入这一切的孤独的民族志学者开放的唯一方法——也很明显，某些人在确定最喜欢的人（即，总是发出公鸡式的叫声，总是启动这个过程）和指导赔率的变化方面都处于领先地位，这些“意见领袖”是下面讨论的更有成就的斗鸡士兼固体公民。如果这些人开始改变他们的主张，其他人也会效仿。如果他们开始下注，其他人也开始下注，尽管总是有大量沮丧的下注者哭着要求更短或更长的赔率到最后，但这种运动或多或少会停止。但对整个过程的详细理解等待着一个可惜的是不太可能得到的东西：一个对个人行为进行精确观察的决策理论家。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 16 Assuming only binomial variability, the departure from a fifty-fifty expectation in the 60 ringgits and below case is 1.38 standard deviations, or (in a one-direction test) an 8 in 100 possibility by chance alone; for the below 40 ringgits case it is 1.65 standard deviations, or about 5 in 100. The fact that these departures though real are not extreme merely indicates, again, that even in the smaller fights the tendency to match cocks at least reasonably evenly persists. It is a matter of relative relaxation of the pressures toward equalization, not their elimination. The tendency for high-bet contests to be coin-flip propositions is, of course, even more striking, and suggests the Balinese know quite well what they are about.
blocks.zh: 16 假设只有二项式变异，在 60 林吉特及以下的情况下，与 550 的期望的偏离是 1.38 个标准差，或（在单向测试中）仅偶然的可能性就有 100 分之 8；对于低于 40 林吉特的情况，这一比例为 1.65 个标准差，或大约为 100 分之 5。事实是，这些偏差虽然不是极端的，但再次表明，即使在规模较小的比赛中，公鸡匹配的趋势至少仍然相当均匀。这是一个相对缓解平等压力的问题，而不是消除压力的问题。当然，高赌注竞赛以抛硬币形式进行的趋势更为引人注目，这表明巴厘岛人非常了解它们的含义。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 17 The reduction in wagering in smaller fights (which, of course, feeds on itself; one of the reasons people find small fights uninteresting is that there is less wagering in them, and contrariwise for large ones) takes place in three mutually reinforcing ways. First, there is a simple withdrawal of interest as people wander off to have a cup of coffee or chat with a friend. Second, the Balinese do not mathematically reduce odds, but bet directly in terms of stated odds as such. Thus, for a 9–8 bet, one man wagers 9 ringgits, the other 8; for 5–4, one wagers 5, the other 4. For any given currency unit, like the ringgit, therefore, 6.3 times as much money is involved in a 10–9 bet as in a 2–1 bet, for example, and, as noted, in small fights betting settles toward the longer end. Finally, the bets which are made tend to be one- rather than two-, three-, or in some of the very largest fights, four- or five-finger ones. (The fingers indicate the multiples of the stated bet odds at issue, not absolute figures. Two fingers in a 6–5 situation means a man wants to wager 10 ringgits on the underdog against 12, three in an 8–7 situation, 21 against 24, and so on.)
blocks.zh: 17 小型拳击比赛中投注额的减少（当然，这会自我调节；人们觉得小型拳击比赛无趣的原因之一是小型拳击比赛中的投注额较少，大型拳击比赛则相反）以三种相辅相成的方式发生。首先，当人们去喝杯咖啡或与朋友聊天时，就会失去兴趣。其次，巴厘岛人不会从数学上降低赔率，而是直接按照规定的赔率进行投注。因此，对于 9-8 的投注，一名男子投注 9 令吉，另一名男子投注 8 令吉；例如，对于 5-4，一个人下注 5，另一个下注 4。因此，对于任何给定的货币单位（如林吉特），10-9 投注所涉及的资金是 2-1 投注的 6.3 倍，并且，如前所述，在小规模战斗中，投注会倾向于长期结算。最后，所下的赌注往往是一指，而不是两指、三指，或者在一些规模最大的比赛中，四指或五指下注。 （手指表示有争议的投注赔率的倍数，而不是绝对数字。在 6-5 的情况下，两根手指意味着一个人想在失败者对 12 人下注 10 林吉特，在 8-7 情况下下注 3 林吉特，在 21 对 24 情况下下注 21 林吉特，依此类推。）
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: 18 Besides wagering there are other economic aspects of the cockfight, especially its very close connection with the local market system which, though secondary both to its motivation and to its function, are not without importance. Cockfights are open events to which anyone who wishes may come, sometimes from quite distant areas, but well over 90 percent, probably over 95, are very local affairs, and the locality concerned is defined not by the village, nor even by the administrative district, but by the rural market system. Bali has a three-day market week with the familiar “solar-system” type rotation. Though the markets themselves have never been very highly developed, small morning affairs in a village square, it is the microregion such rotation rather generally marks out –ten or twenty square miles, seven or eight neighboring villages (which in contemporary Bali is usually going to mean anywhere from five to ten or eleven thousand people) from which the core of any cockfight audience, indeed virtually all of it, will come. Most of the fights are in fact organized and sponsored by small combines of petty rural merchants under the general premise, very strongly held by them and indeed by all Balinese, that cockfights are good for trade because “they get money out of the house, they make it circulate.” Stalls selling various sorts of things as well as assorted sheerchance gambling games (see below) are set up around the edge of the area so that this even takes on the quality of a small fair. This connection of cockfighting with markets and market sellers is very old, as, among other things, their conjunction in inscriptions (Roelof Goris, Prasasti Bali, 2 vols. [Bandung: N. V. Masa Baru, 1954]) indicates. Trade has followed the cock for centuries in rural Bali and the sport has been one of the main agencies of the island’s monetization.
blocks.zh: 18 除了投注之外，斗鸡还有其他经济方面，特别是它与当地市场体系的密切联系，尽管其动机和功能都是次要的，但并非没有重要性。斗鸡是公开活动，任何愿意参加的人都可以参加，有时来自很远的地区，但百分之九十以上，甚至可能超过百分之九十五，都是非常地方性的活动，而且所涉及的地方不是由村庄，甚至不是由行政区划定的，而是由农村市场体系来划定的。巴厘岛有为期三天的市场周，具有熟悉的“太阳系”式轮换。尽管市场本身从来都不是高度发达的，在村庄广场上举行的小型晨间活动，但这种轮换通常标志着一个小区域——十或二十平方英里，七八个邻近的村庄（在当代巴厘岛通常意味着五到一万或一万一千人），任何斗鸡观众的核心，实际上是所有斗鸡观众，都将来自这里。事实上，大多数斗鸡活动都是由农村小商人的小型联合体组织和赞助的，其总体前提是斗鸡有利于贸易，因为“斗鸡可以从家里赚钱，可以流通”，他们甚至所有巴厘岛人都强烈支持斗鸡。出售各种物品的摊位以及各种赌博游戏（见下文）都设置在该区域的边缘，因此甚至具有小型集市的质量。斗鸡与市场和市场卖家的这种联系非常古老，除其他外，它们在铭文中的结合（Roelof Goris，Prasasti Bali，2 卷。[万隆：N.V.Masa Baru，1954]）表明了这一点。几个世纪以来，巴厘岛乡村的贸易一直跟随公鸡的脚步这项运动一直是该岛货币化的主要机构之一。

blocks.en: 20 Of course, even in Bentham, utility is not normally confined as a concept to monetary losses and gains, and my argument here might be more carefully put in terms of a denial that for the Balinese, as for any people, utility (pleasure, happiness . . . ) is merely identifiable with wealth. But such terminological problems are in any case secondary to the essential point: the cockfight is not roulette.
blocks.zh: 20 当然，即使在边沁看来，效用通常也不局限于金钱损失和收益的概念，我在这里的论点可能会更谨慎地表达为否认对于巴厘岛人来说，就像对任何人一样，效用（快乐、幸福……）只能与财富等同。但无论如何，这些术语问题对于关键点来说都是次要的：斗鸡不是轮盘赌。

blocks.en: 21 Max Weber, The Sociology of Religion (Boston: Beacon Press, 1963). There is nothing specifically Balinese, of course, about deepening significance with money, as Whyte’s description of corner boys in a working-class district of Boston demonstrates: “Gambling plays an important role in the lives of Cornerville people. Whatever game the corner boys play, they nearly always bet on the outcome. When there is nothing at stake, the game is not considered a real contest. This does not mean that the financial element is all-important. I have frequently heard men say that the honor of winning was much more important than the money at stake. The corner boys consider playing for money the real test of skill and, unless a man performs well when money is at stake, he is not considered a good competitor.” W. F. Whyte, Street Corner Society, 2d ed. (Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1955), 140.
blocks.zh: 21 马克斯·韦伯，《宗教社会学》（波士顿：灯塔出版社，1963 年）。当然，巴厘岛人并没有什么特别强调金钱的重要性，正如怀特对波士顿工人阶级地区的街角男孩的描述所表明的那样：“赌博在科纳维尔人的生活中发挥着重要作用。无论街角男孩玩什么游戏，他们几乎总是对结果下注。当没有任何利害关系时，游戏就不会被认为是真正的比赛。这并不意味着金钱因素是最重要的。我经常听到人们说获胜的荣誉比金钱更重要。角逐者认为，为了金钱而打球是对技能的真正考验，除非一个人在金钱攸关时表现出色，否则他不会被认为是一个好的竞争者。” W.F.怀特，街角协会，第二版。 （芝加哥：芝加哥大学出版社，1955 年），140。

blocks.en: 22 The extremes to which this madness is conceived on occasion to go–and the fact that it is considered madness–is demonstrated by the Balinese folktale I Tuhung Kuning. A gambler becomes so deranged by his passion that, leaving on a trip, he orders his pregnant wife to take care of the prospective newborn if it is a boy but to feed it as meat to his fighting cocks if it is a girl. The mother gives birth to a girl, but rather than giving the child to the cocks she gives them a large rat and conceals the girl with her own mother. When the husband returns the cocks, crowing a jingle, inform him of the deception and, furious, he sets out to kill the child. A goddess descends from heaven and takes the girl up to the skies with her. The cocks die from the food given them, the owner’s sanity is restored, the goddess brings the girl back to the father who reunites him with his wife. The story is given as “Geel Komkommertje” in Jacoba Hooykaas-van Leeuwen Boomkamp, Sprookjes en Verhalen van Bali (s’Gravenhage: Van Hoeve, 1956), 19–25.
blocks.zh: 22 巴厘岛民间故事 I Tuhung Kuning 证明了这种疯狂有时会走向极端，以及它被认为是疯狂的事实。一个赌徒因激情而变得疯狂，以至于在外出旅行时，他命令怀孕的妻子如果是男孩就照顾即将出生的新生儿，如果是女孩就将其作为肉喂给他的斗鸡。母亲生下了一个女孩，但她没有把孩子交给公鸡，而是给了它们一只大老鼠，并将女孩藏在自己的母亲身边。当丈夫把公鸡送回来时，会鸣叫一声，告诉他他被骗了，他愤怒地打算杀死孩子。一位女神从天而降，带着女孩飞上了天空。公鸡因食物而死，主人恢复了理智，女神将女孩带回父亲身边，父亲又让他与妻子团聚。这个故事在 Jacoba Hooykaas-van Leeuwen Boomkamp, Sprookjes en Verhalen van Bali (s’Gravenhage: Van Hoeve, 1956), 19-25 中被称为“Geel Komkommertje”。

blocks.en: 27 In another of Hooykaas-van Leeuwen Boomkamp’s folk tales (“De Gast,” Sprookjes en Verhalen van Bali, 172–180), a low caste Sudra, a generous, pious, and carefree man who is also an accomplished cockfighter, loses, despite his accomplishment, fight after fight until he is not only out of money but down to his last cock. He does not despair, however–“I bet,” he says, “upon the Unseen World.” His wife, a good and hardworking woman, knowing how much he enjoys cockfighting, gives him her last “rainy day” money to go and bet. But, filled with misgivings due to his run of ill luck, he leaves his own cock at home and bets merely on the side. He soon loses all but a coin or two and repairs to a food stand for a snack, where he meets a decrepit, odorous, and generally unappetizing old beggar leaning on a staff. The old man asks for food, and the hero spends his last coins to buy him some. The old man then asks to pass the night with the hero, which the hero gladly invites him to do. As there is no food in the house, however, the hero tells his wife to kill the last cock for dinner. When the old man discovers this fact, he tells the hero he has three cocks in his own mountain hut and says the hero may have one of them for fighting. He also asks for the hero’s son to accompany him as a servant, and, after the son agrees, this is done. The old man turns out to be Siva and, thus, to live in a great palace in the sky, though the hero does not know this. In time, the hero decides to visit his son and collect the promised cock. Lifted up into Siva’s presence, he is given the choice of three cocks. The first crows: “I have beaten fifteen opponents.” The second crows, “I have beaten twenty-five opponents.” The third crows, “I have beaten the King.” “That one, the third, is my choice,” says the hero, and returns with it to earth. When he arrives at the cockfight, he is asked for an entry fee and replies, “I have no money; I will pay after my cock has won.” As he is known never to win, he is let in because the king, who is there fighting, dislikes him and hopes to enslave him when he loses and cannot pay off. In order to ensure that this happens, the king matches his finest cock against the hero’s. When the cocks are placed down, the hero’s flees, and the crowd, led by the arrogant king, hoots in laughter. The hero’s cock then flies at the king himself, killing him with a spur stab in the throat. The hero flees. His house is encircled by the king’s men. The cock changes into a Garuda, the great mythic bird of Indic legend, and carries the hero and his wife to safety in the heavens. When the people see this, they make the hero king and his wife queen and they return as such to earth. Later their son, released by Siva, also returns and the hero-king announces his intention to enter a hermitage. (“I will fight no more cockfights. I have bet on the Unseen and won.”) He enters the hermitage and his son becomes king.
blocks.zh: 27 在 Hooykaas-van Leeuwen Boomkamp 的另一个民间故事中（“De Gast”，Sprookjes en Verhalen van Bali，172-180），一个低种姓首陀罗，一个慷慨、虔诚、无忧无虑的人，也是一位出色的斗鸡人，尽管他取得了成就，但在一场又一场的战斗中失败了，直到他不仅没钱了，而且只剩下最后一只公鸡了。然而，他并没有绝望——“我打赌，”他说，“赌在看不见的世界上。”他的妻子是一位善良而勤奋的女人，知道他有多喜欢斗鸡，所以给了他最后的“未雨绸缪”的钱去赌。但是，由于运气不好，他充满了疑虑，他把自己的鸡巴留在家里，只做旁注。很快他就失去了所有的东西，只剩下一两枚硬币，于是他来到一个小吃摊买点小吃，在那里他遇到了一个拄着拐杖的、衰弱、臭气熏天、毫无胃口的老乞丐。老人要食物，英雄用掉最后的硬币给他买了一些。然后老人要求与英雄共度一夜，英雄很高兴地邀请他这样做。然而，由于家里没有食物，英雄告诉他的妻子杀死最后一只公鸡作为晚餐。当老人发现这一事实时，他告诉英雄他自己的山间小屋里有三只公鸡，并说英雄可能拥有一只用于战斗。他还请求英雄的儿子作为仆人陪伴他，在儿子同意后，这件事就完成了。老人原来是湿婆，因此住在空中的一座宏伟宫殿里，尽管英雄不知道这一点。及时，英雄决定去看望他的儿子并收集承诺的公鸡。他被举到湿婆面前，可以选择三只雄鸽。第一只乌鸦：“我已经打败了十五个对手。”第二只乌鸦说：“我已经打败了二十五个对手。”第三只乌鸦说：“我打败了国王。” “那一个，第三个，是我的选择。”英雄说道，然后带着它回到了地球。当他到达斗鸡场时，有人向他索要入场费，他回答说：“我没有钱，等我的公鸡获胜后我再付钱。”众所周知，他永远不会赢，所以他被允许进来，因为在那里战斗的国王不喜欢他，并希望在他失败而无法偿还时奴役他。为了确保这一切发生，国王将他最好的鸡巴与英雄的配对。当公鸡被放下时，英雄逃跑了，人群在傲慢的国王的带领下发出笑声。然后英雄的阴茎飞向国王本人，用马刺刺伤了他的喉咙。英雄逃跑了。他的房子被国王的人包围了。公鸡变成了印度传说中的神鸟迦楼罗，将英雄和他的妻子带到了安全的天堂。当人们看到这一点时，他们将英雄国王和他的妻子封为女王，然后他们就这样返回了地球。后来，他们的儿子被湿婆释放，也回来了，英雄王宣布他打算进入隐居。 （“我不会再斗鸡了。我在看不见的东西上打赌并赢了。”）他进入隐居处，他的儿子成为国王。

blocks.en: 28 Addict gamblers are really less declassed (for their status is, as everyone else’s, inherited) than merely impoverished and personally disgraced. The most prominent addict gambler in my cockfight circuit was actually a very high caste satria who sold off most of his considerable lands to support his habit. Though everyone privately regarded him as a fool and worse (some, more charitable, regarded him as sick), he was publicly treated with the elaborate deference and politeness due his rank. On the independence of personal reputation and public status in Bali, see Geertz, Person, Time, and Conduct, 28–35.

blocks.en: 30 British cockfights (the sport was banned there in 1840) indeed seem to have lacked it, and to have generated, therefore, a quite different family of shapes. Most British fights were “mains,” in which a preagreed number of cocks were aligned into two teams and fought serially. Score was kept and wagering took place both on the individual matches and on the main as a whole. There were also “battle Royales,” both in England and on the Continent, in which a large number of cocks were let loose at once with the one left standing at the end the victor. And in Wales, the so-called “Welsh main” followed an elimination pattern, along the lines of a present-day tennis tournament, winners proceeding to the next round. As a genre, the cockfight has perhaps less compositional flexibility than, say, Latin comedy, but it is not entirely without any. On cockfighting more generally, see Arch Ruport, The Art of Cockfighting (New York: Devin-Adair, 1949); G. R. Scott, History of Cockfighting (London: Charles Skilton, 1957); and Lawrence Fitz-Barnard, Fighting Sports (London: Odhams Press, 1921).
blocks.zh: 30 英国斗鸡运动（这项运动于 1840 年在当地被禁止）似乎确实缺乏这种斗鸡运动，因此产生了一个完全不同的斗鸡运动系列。大多数英国比赛都是“主赛”，即预先约定数量的雄鸽分成两队，连续进行比赛。单场比赛和整场比赛均保留比分并进行投注。在英格兰和欧洲大陆也有“大逃杀”活动，大量雄鸽同时被释放，最后剩下的一只获胜。在威尔士，所谓的“威尔士主赛”遵循淘汰赛模式，类似于当今的网球锦标赛，获胜者进入下一轮。作为一种流派，斗鸡的构图灵活性可能不如拉丁喜剧，但也并非完全没有。关于更一般的斗鸡，请参阅 Arch Ruport，《斗鸡的艺术》（纽约：Devin-Adair，1949 年）； G. blocks.en: 34 There are two other Balinese values and disvalues which, connected with punctuate temporality on the one hand and unbridled aggressiveness on the other, reinforce the sense that the cockfight is at once continuous with ordinary social life and a direct negation of it: what the Balinese call ramé, and what they call paling. Ramé means crowded, noisy, and active, and is a highly sought-after social state: crowded markets, mass festivals, busy streets are all ramé as, of course, is, in the extreme, a cockfight. Ramé is what happens in the “full” times (its opposite, sepi, “quiet,” is what happens in the “empty” ones). Paling is social vertigo, the dizzy, disoriented, lost, turned-around feeling one gets when one’s place in the coordinates of social space is not clear, and it is a tremendously disfavored, immensely anxiety-producing state. Balinese regard the exact maintenance of spatial orientation (“not to know where north is” is to be crazy), balance, decorum, status relationships, and so forth, as fundamental to ordered life (krama) and paling, the sort of whirling confusion of position the scrambling cocks exemplify as its profoundest enemy and contradiction. On ramé see Bateson and Mead, Balinese Character, 3, 64; on paling, ibid., 11, and Belo, ed., Traditional Balinese Culture, 90ff.
blocks.zh: 34 巴厘岛还有另外两种价值观和贬义，它们一方面与不经意的时间性有关，另一方面与肆无忌惮的侵略性有关，强化了这样一种感觉：斗鸡既是普通社会生活的延续，又是对它的直接否定：巴厘岛人称之为“ramé”，以及他们所说的“paling”。 Ramé的意思是拥挤、喧闹、活跃，是一种备受追捧的社会状态：拥挤的市场、大型节日、繁忙的街道都是ramé，当然，极端的斗鸡也是如此。 Ramé 是在“充实”的时候发生的事情（它的反面，sepi，“安静”，是在​​“空”的时候发生的事情）。失落是一种社交眩晕症，当一个人在社会空间的坐标中的位置不明确时，就会产生头晕、迷失方向、迷失、转身的感觉，这是一种非常不受欢迎、非常令人焦虑的状态。巴厘岛人将空间方位的精确维持（“不知道北方在哪里”是疯狂的）、平衡、礼仪、地位关系等视为有序生活（krama）的基础，而攀爬公鸡所体现的那种旋转的位置混乱则是其最深刻的敌人和矛盾。关于 ramé，请参阅 Bateson 和 Mead，巴厘岛性格，3, 64； on paling，同上，11，以及 Belo 编辑，传统巴厘岛文化，90ff。

blocks.en: 38 Lévi-Strauss’s “structuralism” might seem an exception. But it is only an apparent one, for, rather than taking myths, totem rites, marriage rules, or whatever as texts to interpret, Lévi-Strauss takes them as ciphers to solve, which is very much not the same thing. He does not seek to understand symbolic forms in terms of how they function in concrete situations to organize perceptions (meanings, emotions, concepts, attitudes); he seeks to understand them entirely in terms of their internal structure, indépendent de tout sujet, de tout objet, et de toute contexte. For my own view of this approach–that is suggestive and indefensible– see Clifford Geertz, “The Cerebral Savage: On the Work of Lévi-Strauss,” Encounter 48 (1967): 25–32.
blocks.zh: 38 列维-斯特劳斯的“结构主义”似乎是一个例外。但这只是表面上的一个，因为列维-斯特劳斯不是把神话、图腾仪式、婚姻规则或其他任何东西当作文本来解释，而是把它们当作密码来解决，这完全不是一回事。他并不试图从符号形式在具体情境中如何发挥作用来组织感知（意义、情感、概​​念、态度）来理解它们；而是试图理解符号形式。他力求完全从其内部结构、独立的总体、总体对象和总体背景的角度来理解它们。对于我自己对这种方法的看法——这是有启发性的和站不住脚的——请参阅 Clifford Geertz, “The Cerebral Savage: On the Work of Lévi-Strauss,” Encounter 48 (1967): 25-32。

blocks.en: 40 The use of the, to Europeans, “natural” visual idiom for perception–“see,” “watches,” and so forth–is more than usually misleading here, for the fact that, as mentioned earlier, Balinese follow the progress of the fight as much (perhaps, as fighting cocks are actually rather hard to see except as blurs of motion, more) with their bodies as with their eyes, moving their limbs, heads, and trunks in gestural mimicry of the cocks’ maneuvers, means that much of the individual’s experience of the fight is kinesthetic rather than visual. If ever there was an example of Kenneth Burke’s definition of a symbolic act as “the dancing of an attitude” (The Philosophy of Literary Form, rev. ed. [New York: Vintage Books, 1957], 9) the cockfight is it. On the enormous role of kinesthetic perception in Balinese life, Bateson and Mead, Balinese Character, 84–88; on the active nature of aesthetic perception in general, Goodman, Language of Art, 241–244.
blocks.zh: 40 对于欧洲人来说，使用“自然”的视觉习语来表达感知——“看”、“手表”等等——在这里比通常情况下更具有误导性，因为事实上，正如前面提到的，巴厘岛人不仅用眼睛来跟踪战斗的进展（也许，斗鸡实际上很难看到，除了运动模糊之外），用他们的身体和眼睛来移动他们的四肢、头部和躯干，模仿斗鸡的动作。公鸡的动作，意味着个人对战斗的大部分体验是动觉的，而不是视觉的。如果肯尼思·伯克将象征性行为定义为“一种态度的舞蹈”（《文学形式哲学》，修订版。[纽约：古着图书，1957]，9），那么斗鸡就是它了。关于动觉知觉在巴厘岛人生活中的巨大作用，贝特森和米德，巴厘岛性格，84-88；关于一般审美知觉的主动本质，古德曼，《艺术语言》，241-244。

blocks.en: 41 All this coupling of the occidental great with the oriental lowly will doubtless disturb certain sorts of aestheticians as the earlier efforts of anthropologists to speak of Christianity and totemism in the same breath disturbed certain sorts of theologians. But as ontological questions are (or should be) bracketed in the sociology of religion, judgmental ones are (or should be) bracketed in the sociology of art. In any case, the attempt to deprovincialize the concept of art is but part of the general anthropological conspiracy to deprovincialize all important social concepts–marriage, religion, law, rationality–and though this is a threat to aesthetic theories which regard certain works of art as beyond the reach of sociological analysis, it is no threat to the conviction, for which Robert Graves claims to have been reprimanded at his Cambridge tripos, that some poems are better than others.

blocks.en: 43 That what the cockfight has to say about Bali is not altogether without perception and the disquiet it expresses about the general pattern of Balinese life is not wholly without reason is attested by the fact that in two weeks of December 1965, during the upheavals following the unsuccessful coup in Djakarta, between forty and eighty thousand Balinese (in a population of about two million) were killed, largely by one another–the worst outburst in the country. (John Hughes, Indonesian Upheaval [New York: McKay, 1967], 173–183. Hughes’s figures are, of course, rather casual estimates, but they are not the most extreme.) This is not to say, of course, that the killings were caused by the cockfight, could have been predicted on the basis of it, or were some sort of enlarged version of it with real people in the place of the cocks–all of which is nonsense. It is merely to say that if one looks at Bali not just through the medium of its dances, its shadowplays, its sculpture, and its girls, but–as the Balinese themselves do–also through the medium of its cockfight, the fact that the massacre occurred seems, if no less appalling, less like a contradiction to the laws of nature. As more than one real Gloucester has discovered, sometimes people actually get life precisely as they most deeply do not want it.
